ERV / transposable-element activity during SC-islet differentiation

Progress report, version 4 · 5 Oct 2026 · repo /pl/active/ZhuLab_BDC/GitHub/HERV_pancreatic_differentiation (Alpine, local git) · local mirror ~/Documents/Claude/HERV_pancreatic_differentiation · outputs $TE_OUT=/scratch/alpine/hzhu10@xsede.org/herv_pancreatic_differentiation/out
New in version 4: provirus vs CDH6 along the endocrine trajectory (5.11). The provirus is the nearest ERV-gene pair to CDH6, which drops at endocrine delamination, so we asked whether the two are linked. They are not: CDH6 falls together with the NEUROG3 rise, well before the provirus switches on; the provirus rises after CHGA, i.e. it marks committed endocrine cells. The provirus–CDH6 anti-correlation is no stronger than for random genes. Also new: Ensembl (GENCODE long-read pipeline) now annotates the provirus as a spliced 2-exon lncRNA, ENSG00000297849, running from its 5′ LTR to its 3′ LTR.
New in version 3: per-copy results (5.10). The endocrine LTR12/HERV9 signal comes from one full-length HERV9 provirus at chr5:30.20 Mb, 1 Mb from any protein-coding gene. Its 5′ LTR opens and the provirus is transcribed from ENP1/ENP2 on, peaking in early EC-β. Several other candidates turn out to be host transcripts (HERV15 in ACSM3, MER92 in a beta-cell lncRNA) or sit in an unmappable duplication (chr5q13). MER11 is not switched on copy by copy in the liver-like cells either.
New in version 2:
  • scTEATAC fixed and run on all samples as a second ATAC method (4.5b, 5.7).
  • Candidates sorted into tiers, with every RNA method on equal footing plus ATAC support from both methods (4.12, 5.8).
  • LTRs paired with their internal regions from genome flanks (4.12).
  • Literature context: LTR6/HERVS71 in endoderm is published (5.0).
  • ZNF808 / MER11 check (4.14, 5.9).
  • Per-copy counts started (4.13).

Summary

  • The pipeline works end to end at subfamily level. All 98,236 kept cells (15 samples, D0–D45) now have per-cell TE-subfamily counts for RNA (IRescue, plus scTE in two modes) and for ATAC (Tn5 cut sites on TEs). These counts feed pseudobulk DESeq2 tests: each cell group vs the rest, and each stage vs the rest.
  • Two positive controls reproduce published biology.
    • HERVH-int / LTR7, the pluripotency ERV, falls about 40× from D0 to D9 and is open in hPSC and DE.
    • HERVS71 and its LTRs LTR6A/B peak at D4 in definitive endoderm, in both RNA and ATAC. This matches Wu et al. 2022 (LTR6B as a FOXA2/GATA4-bound DE enhancer) and Babarinde et al. 2025 (endoderm-specific LTR6A transcripts).
  • Headline: one HERV9 provirus switches on at endocrine induction. chr5:30,197,738–30,205,134 (+) has the structure LTR12B – HERV9NC/HERV9-int – LTR12_ and lies 1 Mb from the nearest protein-coding gene.
    • RNA: zero from hPSC to FG; first seen in ENP1 (26 per million gene UMIs), ENP2 160, early EC-β 396, early δ 252; lower in late endocrine cells (29–108).
    • ATAC: its 5′ LTR is closed to PP2 and opens in the same groups (ENP2 9, early EC-β 16 per million cut sites), in every unit.
    • This one copy is 90–97% of the subfamily-level "LTR12_/HERV9 in endocrine" call.
  • New, robust programs at later stages. Each is called by IRescue or scTE, confirmed by the other, and survives the read-through filter:
    • Pancreatic progenitors: HERV15-int in PP1/PP2, with its LTR (LTR15) more open in PP. This is genuine, but most of the 20× increase is still genic.
    • Endocrine progenitors and early endocrine cells: LTR12_ / LTR12E / HERV9, where 80–90% of reads come from copies outside genes, plus MLT1F2-int. RNA only; their chromatin does not change.
    • Off-target liver-like cells: HERVIP10B3 / LTR10B and PABL_A, transcribed and open.
  • Endocrine-specific opening without transcription. LTR22 / LTR22B gain accessibility in ENP3 and most early endocrine groups (β, α, δ, EC-β; D22–D45) but are not transcribed. They are candidate enhancers.
  • Likely read-through, not ERV transcription: MER92-int and MER110-int in late beta / EC-beta, LTR48B in ENP, LTR19C / LTR25-int in PP2, HERVK-int in OTX2_endo. MER110-int in ENP is "scTE only", probably antisense.
  • Both ATAC methods agree (r = 0.95). scTEATAC's multi-mapping reads add signal only to L1HS / SVA / Alu, not to ERV candidates.
  • ZNF808/MER11: the liver-like off-target cells do not look like ZNF808 loss at subfamily level. ZNF808 is not lower there and MER11 is not higher. A per-copy check is pending.
  • Next: name the induced copies (per-copy counts are running), motifs in LTR12 / LTR22 / LTR15, and the ZNF808 per-copy check.

1. Question and data

Question. Are endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) and other repeats of viral origin switched on at specific stages, or in specific cell types, as human stem cells differentiate into islet cells (SC-islets)? ERVs make up about 8% of the human genome. Most copies are silenced, but some LTRs act as stage-specific promoters and enhancers in early development. HERVH/LTR7 in pluripotent cells is the textbook case. We want to know whether the same thing happens on the way to beta cells, and in which lineages.

Data. The diff-multiome 10x Multiome time course: RNA and ATAC measured in the same nuclei. There are 15 samples over 8 stages (D0 hPSC → D45 SC-islets) from three differentiation batches (HZ015, HZ019/HZ021, XW002). Cell annotation comes from the shared single-cell-pipeline: ATAC_WNN_annotation, using only cells with include_downstream == True, 98,236 cells in 24 groups. This project reads those shared inputs through config.sh and never copies or writes into them.

2. Why TE quantification in single-nucleus multiome is tricky

Every design choice below exists to deal with one of these five problems.

ProblemWhat goes wrongHow we handle it
Multi-mapping readsYoung ERVs (HERVK HML-2, young HERVH, L1HS) have thousands of nearly identical copies. Reads land equally well on many of them, so aligners give them low MAPQ. Discarding multi-mappers removes exactly the elements of most interest.Count at the subfamily level first, where a read compatible with many copies of one subfamily is still unambiguous. IRescue resolves reads that fit several subfamilies with an EM step.
Intronic read-throughSingle-nucleus RNA is full of unspliced pre-mRNA. Most TEs sit in introns, so a transcribed host gene puts reads on its intronic ERVs. A cell type that expresses that gene then looks as if it "induces" the ERV.scTE with two indexes: exclusive (intronic TE reads kept) vs nointron (only TE reads outside genes). Calls that vanish in nointron are flagged. Locus-level host-gene checks come next.
3′ chemistry10x 3′ GEX only captures the 3′ end of polyadenylated transcripts. An ERV transcript is seen only if its polyA site is captured, and we see roughly where it ends, not where it starts.We keep strand information (forward-stranded) in IRescue. Locus-level work will look at read position relative to the LTR.
ATAC mappabilityCell Ranger fragments keep only MAPQ ≥ 30 reads. ATAC signal on young, repetitive elements is therefore under-counted and comes mostly from older, more diverged copies.Interpret ATAC on young families (LTR5_Hs, LTR7) cautiously; absence of ATAC signal is weak evidence.
Stage = cell type = batchEarly cell types exist in only one sample (hPSC only at D0, DE mostly at D4). Stage and differentiation batch coincide for most stages; only D7 and D9 have two batches.DESeq2 uses ~ group without a sample term, because blocking on sample would remove the contrasts we care about. P-values are therefore optimistic. Effect size and consistency across modalities matter more than padj.

4. Methods, step by step

Each step lists what it does, why we need it, how it works, and the gotchas we hit. The full script is in the collapsible block under each step, copied verbatim from the repo.

4.0 Environment and repeat annotation

What
Builds the herv_te conda env (IRescue 1.2.0, scTE, samtools, bedtools, pychromvar, scanpy). Downloads the UCSC RepeatMasker table for hg38.
Why
No TE tools existed on Alpine. RepeatMasker is the standard TE annotation and defines what a "subfamily" is (e.g. HERVH-int = internal region of HERVH, LTR7 = its LTR).
How
UCSC rmsk.txt.gz is converted to a BED with subfamily, strand, family and class (rmsk_hg38.bed.gz), plus an LTR-only subset. The env is built on acompile, which has internet access. scTE is patched because it opens files with mode 'rU', which Python 3.11 rejects.
Output
/pl/active/ZhuLab_BDC/genome/repeats_hg38/, env at /projects/hzhu10@xsede.org/software/anaconda/envs/herv_te
envs/get_repeat_annotations.sh
#!/bin/bash
# Download the hg38 RepeatMasker annotation (UCSC rmsk table) into $TE_ANNOT_DIR and make:
#   rmsk_hg38.bed.gz      all repeats: chrom start end name(subfamily) score strand family class
#   rmsk_hg38_ERV.bed.gz  LTR-class repeats only (ERV1, ERVK, ERVL, ERVL-MaLR, Gypsy, unknown LTR)
# Source: https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/hg38/database/rmsk.txt.gz (~160 MB)
set -euo pipefail
source "$(dirname "$0")/../config.sh"
mkdir -p "$TE_ANNOT_DIR"; cd "$TE_ANNOT_DIR"
[ -s rmsk.txt.gz ] || wget -q https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/hg38/database/rmsk.txt.gz
# UCSC rmsk columns: 6 genoName 7 genoStart 8 genoEnd 10 strand 11 repName 12 repClass 13 repFamily
zcat rmsk.txt.gz | awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"} $6 !~ /_/ {print $6,$7,$8,$11,$2,$10,$13,$12}' \
  | sort -k1,1 -k2,2n | gzip > rmsk_hg38.bed.gz
zcat rmsk_hg38.bed.gz | awk '$8=="LTR"' | gzip > rmsk_hg38_ERV.bed.gz
echo "repeats: $(zcat rmsk_hg38.bed.gz | wc -l); LTR/ERV: $(zcat rmsk_hg38_ERV.bed.gz | wc -l)"
zcat rmsk_hg38_ERV.bed.gz | cut -f7 | sort | uniq -c | sort -k1,1nr
envs/build_herv_te_env.sh
#!/bin/bash
# Build the TE-analysis environment (herv_te). Run on a compute node (srun) or the login node.
#   conda/bioconda: python 3.11, samtools, bedtools, pysam
#   PyPI:           IRescue (subfamily TE counts for 10x, UMI-aware EM), pychromvar, scanpy
#   GitHub:         scTE (JiekaiLab/scTE), installed from source
# Stellarscope (locus level) is added in a second step, once the subfamily analysis is running.
set -euo pipefail
source "$(dirname "$0")/../config.sh"
MM=/projects/hzhu10@xsede.org/software/micromamba_bootstrap/bin/micromamba
export MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX=/projects/hzhu10@xsede.org/software/micromamba_root

"$MM" create -y -p "$TE_ENV" -c conda-forge -c bioconda \
  python=3.11 samtools bedtools pysam pip git
"$TE_ENV/bin/pip" install --no-cache-dir irescue pychromvar scanpy anndata pandas numpy scipy
"$TE_ENV/bin/pip" install --no-cache-dir "git+https://github.com/JiekaiLab/scTE.git"
# scTE opens files with mode 'rU', which Python >= 3.11 rejects ("invalid mode: 'rU'"); 'r' is the
# Python 3 equivalent (universal newlines are the default).
sed -i "s/'rU'/'r'/g" "$TE_ENV/bin/scTE_build" "$TE_ENV"/lib/python3.11/site-packages/scTE/annotation.py

echo "--- versions"
"$TE_ENV/bin/irescue" --version || true
"$TE_ENV/bin/python" -c "import pychromvar, scanpy; print('pychromvar', pychromvar.__version__, 'scanpy', scanpy.__version__)"
"$TE_ENV/bin/scTE" -h | head -3 || true
"$TE_ENV/bin/samtools" --version | head -1

4.1 scTE indexes and the TE BED

What
Writes the TE BED used by every counting step: 4,516,048 loci in 1,090 subfamilies, limited to the classes LTR, LINE, SINE, DNA, Retroposon and RC. It also builds the scTE genome indexes in two modes.
Why
One shared definition of "TE" keeps IRescue, scTE and ATAC comparable. Simple repeats, satellites and small-RNA genes are not TEs and would add noise. The two scTE modes are what let us separate ERV transcription from intronic read-through later (4.10).
How
scTE splits the genome into bins and records which gene or TE each bin belongs to. It assigns reads to genes first, then to TEs. In exclusive mode, a read on a TE inside a gene exon goes to the gene, but intronic and intergenic TE reads go to the TE. In nointron mode, any read inside a gene body (exon or intron) goes to the gene, so only TE reads outside genes count as TE. Gene models come from the Cell Ranger ARC GRCh38-2020-A GTF, so genes match the main analysis.
Gotcha
scTE_build -o X writes X.<mode>.idx, so symlinks hg38.<mode>.idx were added. The scTEATAC index was built but later abandoned (see 4.5).
scripts/01_build_scte_indexes.sh
#!/bin/bash
# Build the scTE indexes (subfamily level) from RepeatMasker hg38 + the Cell Ranger ARC GRCh38 GTF.
#   TE BED (6 columns, name = subfamily): transposable-element classes only
#     (LTR, LINE, SINE, DNA, Retroposon, RC, incl. "?"-uncertain calls); simple repeats,
#     low complexity, satellites and small-RNA genes are left out.
#   RNA indexes (scTE_build): exclusive (drop reads on exons of coding genes / lncRNAs) and
#     nointron (also drop reads inside introns; intergenic TE reads only) -- comparing the two
#     separates autonomous TE transcription from host-gene read-through in single-nucleus data.
#   ATAC index (scTEATAC_build): TE BED only.
# Outputs: $TE_ANNOT_DIR/scte/  (hg38_TE.bed, hg38.exclusive.idx, hg38.nointron.idx, hg38.te_atac.idx)
set -euo pipefail
source "$(dirname "$0")/../config.sh"
out="$TE_ANNOT_DIR/scte"; mkdir -p "$out"; cd "$out"

zcat "$TE_ANNOT_DIR/rmsk_hg38.bed.gz" \
  | awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"} {c=$8; sub(/\?$/,"",c)} c ~ /^(LTR|LINE|SINE|DNA|Retroposon|RC)$/ {print $1,$2,$3,$4,$5,$6}' \
  > hg38_TE.bed
echo "TE loci: $(wc -l < hg38_TE.bed); subfamilies: $(cut -f4 hg38_TE.bed | sort -u | wc -l)"

gtf="$out/genes.gtf"
[ -s "$gtf" ] || zcat "$CELLRANGER_REF/genes/genes.gtf.gz" > "$gtf"

for mode in exclusive nointron; do
  # scTE_build appends ".<mode>.idx" to -o itself, so -o hg38.<mode> gives hg38.<mode>.<mode>.idx;
  # link the name the counting jobs use (hg38.<mode>.idx)
  "$TE_ENV/bin/scTE_build" -te hg38_TE.bed -gene "$gtf" -m "$mode" -g other -o "hg38.$mode"
  ln -sfn "hg38.$mode.$mode.idx" "hg38.$mode.idx"
done
"$TE_ENV/bin/scTEATAC_build" -g hg38_TE.bed -o hg38.te_atac
ls -la "$out"

4.2 Sample table and cell whitelists

What
Maps each Cell Ranger run to its analysis name (e.g. HZ180_…_hPSC_rep1 → HZ015_D0_rep1). Writes one barcode whitelist per sample with the kept, annotated cells.
Why
Counting only the 98,236 QC-passed cells makes every TE matrix line up with the annotation. It also makes the jobs much faster, because BAMs are filtered to these cells.
How
Reads the rename manifest and the annotation CSV, and keeps include_downstream == True. Barcodes are stored as in the BAM CB tag (AAAC…-1). In the merged objects a cell is named <sample>#<barcode>.
Output
configs/samples.tsv (task id = SLURM array index), $TE_OUT/whitelists/<sample>.txt
scripts/02_make_sample_table.py
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
Sample table and per-sample cell whitelists for the TE counting jobs.

Reads the diff-multiome sample manifest (Cell Ranger folder -> analysis name) and the shared
annotation table; keeps cells with include_downstream == True.
Writes:
  configs/samples.tsv             task, sample, cellranger_folder, gex_bam, atac_bam, n_cells
  $TE_OUT/whitelists/<sample>.txt barcodes (as in the BAM CB tag, e.g. AAAC...-1), one per line
Usage: python scripts/02_make_sample_table.py   (paths from config.sh via environment)
"""
import os
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

repo = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
cfg = {}
for line in (repo / "config.sh").read_text().splitlines():
    if "=" in line and not line.lstrip().startswith(("#", "mkdir")):
        k, v = line.split("=", 1)
        cfg[k.strip()] = os.path.expandvars(v.split("#")[0].strip().strip('"').replace("$", "$"))
for k in list(cfg):  # resolve ${VAR} references between config entries
    for kk, vv in cfg.items():
        cfg[k] = cfg[k].replace(f"${kk}", vv)

man = pd.read_csv(cfg["SAMPLE_MANIFEST"]).query("status == 'ok'").sort_values("new_name")
ann = pd.read_csv(cfg["ANNOTATION_CSV"], index_col=0, dtype=str)
ann = ann[ann.include_downstream.str.lower() == "true"]
wl_dir = Path(cfg["TE_OUT"]) / "whitelists"; wl_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

rows = []
for i, r in enumerate(man.itertuples(), start=1):
    outs = next(Path(d) / r.old_name / "outs" for d in cfg["CELLRANGER_DIRS"].split()
                if (Path(d) / r.old_name / "outs").is_dir())
    bc = [b.split("#", 1)[1] for b in ann.index if b.startswith(r.new_name + "#")]
    (wl_dir / f"{r.new_name}.txt").write_text("\n".join(bc) + "\n")
    rows.append({"task": i, "sample": r.new_name, "cellranger_folder": r.old_name,
                 "gex_bam": outs / "gex_possorted_bam.bam", "atac_bam": outs / "atac_possorted_bam.bam",
                 "n_cells": len(bc)})
tab = pd.DataFrame(rows)
(repo / "configs").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
tab.to_csv(repo / "configs" / "samples.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)
print(tab[["task", "sample", "cellranger_folder", "n_cells"]].to_string(index=False))
print("total cells:", tab.n_cells.sum())

4.3 RNA: IRescue subfamily counts (main RNA quantification)

What
Builds a per-cell, per-subfamily UMI count matrix from each GEX BAM.
Why
IRescue is built for 10x data and TEs. It works with UMIs (deduplicated molecules, not reads) and keeps multi-mapping reads. Reads that fit several subfamilies are shared out statistically instead of being thrown away.
How
  1. For every read from a whitelisted cell, collect all its alignments (Cell Ranger keeps secondary alignments of multi-mappers). Record the set of TE subfamilies they overlap on the correct strand.
  2. Group reads by cell barcode (CB) and corrected UMI (UB). One UMI = one molecule, so PCR duplicates collapse.
  3. A UMI compatible with one subfamily is assigned directly. A UMI compatible with several (an "equivalence class") is shared by expectation–maximisation: start from the unique counts, assign ambiguous UMIs in proportion to each subfamily's current abundance in that cell, re-estimate, and repeat until stable. --integers rounds the result.
  4. --strandedness forward: in 10x 3′ GEX, read 2 is in the sense of the mRNA, so only reads on the TE's own strand count as that TE. Antisense reads, typically from a host gene running the other way, are not counted.
Output
$TE_OUT/irescue_subfamily/<sample>/counts/ (MTX)
scripts/03_irescue_subfamily.sb
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --mem=40G
#SBATCH --time=12:00:00
#SBATCH --partition=acpu
#SBATCH --qos=cpu-normal
#SBATCH --array=1-15%8
#SBATCH --job-name=irescue
#SBATCH --output=logs/irescue.%A_%a.out
# IRescue, subfamily level, one sample per array task. Cells: whitelist of kept annotated cells.
# 10x 3' GEX is forward-stranded (read 2 is sense), so sense and antisense TE reads are separated.
# UB = Cell Ranger's corrected UMI. Usage (repo root): sbatch scripts/03_irescue_subfamily.sb
set -euo pipefail
source config.sh
mkdir -p logs
row=$(awk -F'\t' -v t="${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}" 'NR>1 && $1==t' configs/samples.tsv)
sample=$(cut -f2 <<<"$row"); gex_bam=$(cut -f4 <<<"$row"); atac_bam=$(cut -f5 <<<"$row")
wl="$TE_OUT/whitelists/${sample}.txt"
export PATH="$TE_ENV/bin:$PATH"
echo "task ${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}: ${sample} ($(wc -l < "$wl") cells)"
out="$TE_OUT/irescue_subfamily/${sample}"; mkdir -p "$out"
irescue -b "$gex_bam" -r "$TE_ANNOT_DIR/scte/hg38_TE.bed" -w "$wl" -c CB -u UB \
  --strandedness forward --integers -p "$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK" -o "$out" -v
ls -la "$out"

4.4 RNA: scTE counts (cross-check and read-through test)

What
Gene + TE count matrices from scTE, once with the exclusive index and once with the nointron index.
Why
It is an independent algorithm, so it checks IRescue. More importantly, the two indexes give an "intergenic only" version of every subfamily.
How
The BAM is first filtered to whitelisted cells, keeping only reads that have a corrected UMI (samtools view -D CB:whitelist -e 'exists([UB])'). scTE then assigns each read to a gene or TE through the index, counts UMIs per cell, and sums TE loci by subfamily. scTE is not strand-aware for TEs, so it also counts antisense reads. That is one reason its TE counts are higher than IRescue's.
Gotchas
scTE stops on reads without CB/UB, hence the filter. Each worker loads the whole index (~200 GB peak in total), so this runs on amem with 6 workers and 320 GB. On acpu with 60–80 GB it ran out of memory. Run time was 30–85 min per sample; job 33356420, plus 33356418_10 for sample 10.
scripts/04_scte_rna.sb
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=6
#SBATCH --mem=320G
#SBATCH --time=24:00:00
#SBATCH --partition=amem
#SBATCH --qos=mem-normal
#SBATCH --array=1-15%4
#SBATCH --job-name=scte_rna
#SBATCH --output=logs/scte_rna.%A_%a.out
# Runs on amem: scTE workers (one per chromosome batch) each load the full TE index; 8 workers in
# 60-80 GB were OOM-killed, so 6 workers in 320 GB.
# scTE on the GEX BAM, subfamily level, with both indexes: exclusive (drops reads on exons of coding
# genes / lncRNAs) and nointron (also drops intronic reads). CB/UB = Cell Ranger corrected tags.
# scTE has no whitelist option; kept cells are selected afterwards. Usage: sbatch scripts/04_scte_rna.sb
set -euo pipefail
source config.sh
mkdir -p logs
row=$(awk -F'\t' -v t="${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}" 'NR>1 && $1==t' configs/samples.tsv)
sample=$(cut -f2 <<<"$row"); gex_bam=$(cut -f4 <<<"$row"); atac_bam=$(cut -f5 <<<"$row")
wl="$TE_OUT/whitelists/${sample}.txt"
export PATH="$TE_ENV/bin:$PATH"
echo "task ${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}: ${sample} ($(wc -l < "$wl") cells)"
# scTE refuses a BAM whose first reads have no CB tag (Cell Ranger keeps reads without a cell);
# keep only reads from the whitelisted cells (also much smaller and faster), on scratch, removed at exit
tmpd="$TE_OUT/tmp_bam/${SLURM_JOB_ID}"; mkdir -p "$tmpd"; trap 'rm -rf "$tmpd"' EXIT
fbam="$tmpd/${sample}.cells.bam"
# reads must also carry a corrected UMI (UB); scTE stops on reads without one
samtools view -@ "$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK" -b -D "CB:$wl" -e 'exists([UB])' -o "$fbam" "$gex_bam"
samtools index -@ "$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK" "$fbam"
echo "filtered BAM: $(du -h "$fbam" | cut -f1)"
for mode in exclusive nointron; do
  out="$TE_OUT/scte_rna_${mode}"; mkdir -p "$out"; cd "$out"
  scTE -i "$fbam" -x "$TE_ANNOT_DIR/scte/hg38.${mode}.idx" -o "${sample}" -CB CB -UMI UB \
    --hdf5 True -p "$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK" --min_genes 200 --expect-cells 15000
  cd - >/dev/null
done

4.5 ATAC: TE-subfamily accessibility from fragments

What
For every cell, counts Tn5 cut sites falling in each TE subfamily, plus the cell's total cut sites.
Why
Chromatin opening of an LTR is the regulatory counterpart of its transcription. It is often the more direct readout of an LTR acting as an enhancer or promoter, and it does not suffer from intronic read-through.
How
Each ATAC fragment has two Tn5 insertion (cut) sites, at its start and at its end − 1. The script keeps fragments from whitelisted cells, turns each into its two cut sites, intersects them with the TE BED (bedtools intersect), and sums per cell × subfamily. A cut site inside nested TEs counts once for each TE. Cell totals are kept for normalisation. Overall, 26.9% of all cut sites fall in TEs.
Note
Cell Ranger fragment files hold only reads with MAPQ ≥ 30, so reads that map to several copies are missing here. scTEATAC (4.5b) keeps them, and 4.11 compares the two.
scripts/05_atac_te_counts.sb
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4
#SBATCH --mem=24G
#SBATCH --time=08:00:00
#SBATCH --partition=acpu
#SBATCH --qos=cpu-normal
#SBATCH --array=1-15%8
#SBATCH --job-name=atac_te
#SBATCH --output=logs/atac_te.%A_%a.out
# Per-cell TE-subfamily accessibility from the Cell Ranger ARC fragment files (replaces scTEATAC, which
# takes the cell barcode from the read name -- not where Cell Ranger puts it -- and collapsed the
# data into 2 "cells").
#   1. keep fragments of the whitelisted cells (barcodes are GEX-matched, as in the RNA)
#   2. each fragment -> its two Tn5 cut sites (start, end-1)
#   3. bedtools intersect cut sites with the TE BED (4.5 M loci, subfamily = column 4); a cut site
#      inside nested TEs counts once for each overlapping TE
#   4. sum per cell x subfamily; also total cut sites per cell (for normalisation)
# Output: $TE_OUT/atac_te_subfamily/<sample>.counts.tsv.gz  (barcode, subfamily, cut_sites)
#         $TE_OUT/atac_te_subfamily/<sample>.cell_totals.tsv  (barcode, total_cut_sites, te_cut_sites)
# Usage (repo root): sbatch scripts/05_atac_te_counts.sb
set -euo pipefail
source config.sh
row=$(awk -F'\t' -v t="${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}" 'NR>1 && $1==t' configs/samples.tsv)
sample=$(cut -f2 <<<"$row"); atac_bam=$(cut -f5 <<<"$row")
frag="$(dirname "$atac_bam")/atac_fragments.tsv.gz"
wl="$TE_OUT/whitelists/${sample}.txt"
export PATH="$TE_ENV/bin:$PATH"
out="$TE_OUT/atac_te_subfamily"; mkdir -p "$out"
echo "task ${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}: ${sample} ($(wc -l < "$wl") cells) from $frag"

zcat "$frag" | awk -F'\t' -v OFS='\t' -v wl="$wl" -v tot="$out/${sample}.totals.tmp" '
  BEGIN { while ((getline b < wl) > 0) keep[b] = 1 }
  /^#/ { next }
  ($4 in keep) { print $1, $2, $2 + 1, $4; print $1, $3 - 1, $3, $4; n[$4] += 2 }
  END { for (b in n) print b, n[b] > tot }' \
| bedtools intersect -a stdin -b "$TE_ANNOT_DIR/scte/hg38_TE.bed" -wa -wb \
| awk -F'\t' -v OFS='\t' '{ c[$4 "\t" $8]++ } END { for (k in c) print k, c[k] }' \
| gzip > "$out/${sample}.counts.tsv.gz"

# totals per cell: all cut sites, and cut sites in any TE (sum over subfamilies)
zcat "$out/${sample}.counts.tsv.gz" | awk -F'\t' -v OFS='\t' '{ t[$1] += $3 } END { for (b in t) print b, t[b] }' \
  | sort > "$out/${sample}.te.tmp"
sort "$out/${sample}.totals.tmp" | join -t $'\t' -a 1 -e 0 -o 0,1.2,2.2 - "$out/${sample}.te.tmp" \
  | awk -v OFS='\t' 'BEGIN { print "barcode", "total_cut_sites", "te_cut_sites" } { print }' > "$out/${sample}.cell_totals.tsv"
rm -f "$out/${sample}.totals.tmp" "$out/${sample}.te.tmp"
echo "cells: $(($(wc -l < "$out/${sample}.cell_totals.tsv") - 1)); rows: $(zcat "$out/${sample}.counts.tsv.gz" | wc -l)"
awk -F'\t' 'NR > 1 { a += $2; b += $3 } END { printf "cut sites: %d total, %d in TEs (%.1f%%)\n", a, b, 100 * b / a }' "$out/${sample}.cell_totals.tsv"

4.5b ATAC, second method: scTEATAC (fixed)

What
Per-cell TE-subfamily counts from the ATAC BAM using scTE's own ATAC mode. This is an independent, published method that also keeps reads mapping to several copies.
Why it failed first
  1. scTEATAC never reads the CB tag. It runs bamToBed -bedpe | awk -F '[\t:]' '{print $1,$2,$6,$7}', so the "barcode" is the first :-separated piece of the read name. For Cell Ranger reads (LH00368:19:…, A01535:176:…) that is the sequencer ID, so each sample collapsed into 2 "cells".
  2. bamToBed -bedpe needs mates next to each other, i.e. a name-sorted BAM. The coordinate-sorted BAM produced thousands of "mate does not occur next to it… skipping" warnings and lost reads.
Fix
  1. Keep whitelisted proper pairs, dropping unmapped, secondary, supplementary and duplicate reads (-f 2 -F 0xD0C). Keep reads of every MAPQ.
  2. Put the cell barcode in front of each read name (AAAC…-1:LH00368:…).
  3. Name-sort, then run scTEATAC with -CB True.
Tested first on a small region: the left mate always came first and no pairs crossed chromosomes. Result: every whitelisted cell is recovered in all 15 samples and there are 0 mate warnings.
How it counts
Each fragment, from mate 1 start to mate 2 end, adds 1 to every TE copy it overlaps. That is the whole fragment span, not just the Tn5 cut sites. Reads that map to several copies sit on the one copy the aligner picked.
Cost
20–50 min and ~175 GB per sample on amem; each scTE worker loads the whole index.
scripts/05b_scte_atac.sb
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=6
#SBATCH --mem=320G
#SBATCH --time=24:00:00
#SBATCH --partition=amem
#SBATCH --qos=mem-normal
#SBATCH --array=1-15%4
#SBATCH --job-name=scte_atac
#SBATCH --output=logs/scte_atac.%A_%a.out
# scTEATAC on the Cell Ranger ARC ATAC BAM, made to work (the first attempt, archive_05_scte_atac.sb,
# collapsed each sample into 2 "cells"):
#   - scTEATAC never reads the CB tag. It runs `bamToBed -bedpe | awk -F '[\t:]' '{print $1,$2,$6,$7}'`,
#     so the barcode is the first ':'-field of the read name (for Cell Ranger: the sequencer ID).
#     -> prefix every read name with its CB: "AAAC...-1:LH00368:19:...".
#   - bamToBed -bedpe needs mates next to each other -> name-sort (coordinate order skipped most pairs).
#     Name-sorted, bamToBed reports the leftmost mate first, so start1..end2 is the fragment.
#   - keep proper pairs only; drop unmapped, secondary, supplementary and duplicate reads (-f 2 -F 0xD0C).
#     All MAPQ are kept: multi-mapping reads (MAPQ < 30, ~6%) sit on one random copy, which is fine at
#     subfamily level -- these reads are absent from the fragment files used by 05_atac_te_counts.sb.
# Counting (scTE): every TE locus overlapped by the whole fragment (not only its Tn5 cut sites) adds 1
# to that locus' subfamily; cells are already whitelisted, so --min_counts 1.
# Output: $TE_OUT/scte_atac/<sample>.h5ad. Usage: sbatch [--array=10] scripts/05b_scte_atac.sb
set -euo pipefail
source config.sh
row=$(awk -F'\t' -v t="${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}" 'NR>1 && $1==t' configs/samples.tsv)
sample=$(cut -f2 <<<"$row"); atac_bam=$(cut -f5 <<<"$row")
wl="$TE_OUT/whitelists/${sample}.txt"
export PATH="$TE_ENV/bin:$PATH"
echo "task ${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}: ${sample} ($(wc -l < "$wl") cells)"
tmpd="$TE_OUT/tmp_bam/${SLURM_JOB_ID}_${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}"; mkdir -p "$tmpd"; trap 'rm -rf "$tmpd"' EXIT
nbam="$tmpd/${sample}.bam"     # file name gives the sample name inside scTE
samtools view -@ 2 -h -f 2 -F 0xD0C -D "CB:$wl" "$atac_bam" \
  | awk -v OFS='\t' '/^@/ { print; next }
      { for (i = 12; i <= NF; i++) if ($i ~ /^CB:Z:/) { $1 = substr($i, 6) ":" $1; break }; print }' \
  | samtools sort -n -@ 4 -m 3G -T "$tmpd/sort" -o "$nbam" -
echo "name-sorted BAM: $(du -h "$nbam" | cut -f1)"
out="$TE_OUT/scte_atac"; mkdir -p "$out"; cd "$out"
scTEATAC -i "$nbam" -x "$TE_ANNOT_DIR/scte/hg38.te_atac.idx" -o "${sample}" -CB True \
  --hdf5 True -p "$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK" --min_counts 1

4.6 Merge IRescue matrices and first look

What
Combines the 15 IRescue matrices into one AnnData (cells × subfamilies). Adds stage, annotation and per-cell gene UMIs, then writes QC tables and figures.
Why
To check that the counts behave sensibly (the HERVH drop after pluripotency, class composition) before running statistics.
How
Feature columns are aligned across samples. Gene UMIs come from the shared integrated RNA object (total_counts). Expression is shown as TE UMIs per million gene UMIs. This is a normalisation, not a "fraction of the transcriptome", because TE reads and gene reads overlap.
Output
irescue_subfamily_merged.h5ad, $TE_OUT/qc/irescue_*
scripts/06_merge_irescue.py
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
Merge the 15 IRescue subfamily matrices into one AnnData and take a first look.

Inputs : $TE_OUT/irescue_subfamily/<sample>/counts/{matrix.mtx.gz,features.tsv.gz,barcodes.tsv.gz}
         shared annotation table (ATAC_WNN_annotation, stage, include_downstream)
         per-cell gene UMIs (total_counts) from the shared merged RNA object
         RepeatMasker subfamily -> family / class map
Outputs: $TE_OUT/irescue_subfamily/irescue_subfamily_merged.h5ad   (cells x TE subfamilies, raw counts)
         $TE_OUT/qc/irescue_*.csv / .png
   - TE UMIs per cell and per 10k gene UMIs, by stage
   - pseudobulk TE expression (UMIs per million gene UMIs) per stage and per annotation group
   - HERV-H / HERV-K / L1HS / SVA check across stages
   - heatmap of the most variable ERV (LTR-class) subfamilies across annotation groups

Note: TE reads can also be gene reads (intronic TEs in single-nucleus data), so "per gene UMIs" is a
normalisation, not a TE fraction of the transcriptome.
"""
import os
from pathlib import Path

import h5py
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import scipy.io
import scipy.sparse as sp
import anndata as ad

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TE_OUT = Path(os.environ["TE_OUT"]); ANNOT = Path(os.environ["ANNOTATION_CSV"])
SCP_OUT = Path(os.environ["SCP_OUT"]); TE_ANNOT = Path(os.environ["TE_ANNOT_DIR"])
qc = TE_OUT / "qc"; qc.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
STAGES = ["D0", "D4", "D7", "D9", "D12", "D15", "D22", "D45"]
GROUP_ORDER = ["hPSC", "DE", "GT", "OTX2_endo", "FG", "liver", "PP1", "PP2", "ductal", "exocrine", "ENP1", "ENP2",
               "ENP3", "early_SC_beta", "early_EC_beta", "early_SC_alpha", "early_SC_delta", "early_SC_EC",
               "late_SC_beta", "late_EC_beta", "late_SC_alpha", "late_SC_delta", "late_SC_EC", "stroma"]
FOCUS = ["HERVH-int", "LTR7", "LTR7Y", "LTR7B", "HERVK-int", "LTR5_Hs", "HERV9-int", "LTR12C", "MER41B",
         "HERVE-int", "HERVW-int", "LTR17", "L1HS", "L1PA2", "SVA_F", "SVA_D"]

samples = pd.read_csv(REPO / "configs/samples.tsv", sep="\t")
ann = pd.read_csv(ANNOT, index_col=0, dtype=str)

# ---- merge
mats, obs_names, feats = [], [], None
for s in samples["sample"]:
    d = TE_OUT / "irescue_subfamily" / s / "counts"
    m = scipy.io.mmread(d / "matrix.mtx.gz").tocsr().T          # features x cells -> cells x features
    f = pd.read_csv(d / "features.tsv.gz", sep="\t", header=None)[0].astype(str).values
    b = pd.read_csv(d / "barcodes.tsv.gz", header=None)[0].astype(str).values
    df = pd.DataFrame.sparse.from_spmatrix(m, columns=f)  # align feature order across samples
    if feats is None:
        feats = list(f)
    else:
        feats = list(dict.fromkeys(feats + list(f)))
    mats.append((m, f)); obs_names += [f"{s}#{x}" for x in b]
    print(f"{s}: {m.shape[0]} cells, {m.shape[1]} subfamilies, {int(m.sum()):,} TE UMIs", flush=True)
fidx = {f: i for i, f in enumerate(feats)}
blocks = []
for m, f in mats:
    cols = np.array([fidx[x] for x in f])
    m = m.tocoo()
    blocks.append(sp.csr_matrix((m.data, (m.row, cols[m.col])), shape=(m.shape[0], len(feats))))
X = sp.vstack(blocks).tocsr().astype(np.float32)

rm = pd.read_csv(TE_ANNOT / "rmsk_hg38.bed.gz", sep="\t", header=None, usecols=[3, 6, 7],
                 names=["subfamily", "family", "class"]).drop_duplicates("subfamily").set_index("subfamily")
var = pd.DataFrame(index=feats)
var["family"] = rm["family"].reindex(feats).fillna("unknown").values
var["class"] = rm["class"].reindex(feats).fillna("unknown").str.rstrip("?").values

obs = ann.reindex(obs_names)[["stage", "cluster", "single_stage_label", "ATAC_WNN_annotation", "include_downstream"]].copy()
obs["sample"] = [n.split("#")[0] for n in obs_names]
with h5py.File(SCP_OUT / "integration/h5ad/merged_rna_scvi_integrated.h5ad", "r") as h:
    idx = h["obs"]["_index"][:].astype(str)
    gene_umis = pd.Series(h["obs"]["total_counts"][:], index=idx)
obs["gene_umis"] = gene_umis.reindex(obs_names).values
te = ad.AnnData(X=X, obs=obs, var=var)
te.obs["te_umis"] = np.asarray(X.sum(1)).ravel()
te.obs["te_per_10k_gene"] = 1e4 * te.obs.te_umis / te.obs.gene_umis
print(f"merged: {te.n_obs} cells x {te.n_vars} subfamilies; missing annotation: {te.obs.stage.isna().sum()}", flush=True)
te.write_h5ad(TE_OUT / "irescue_subfamily" / "irescue_subfamily_merged.h5ad", compression="gzip")
te = te[te.obs.include_downstream.str.lower() == "true"].copy()

# ---- TE load by stage and class
load = te.obs.groupby("stage")[["te_umis", "gene_umis", "te_per_10k_gene"]].median().reindex(STAGES).round(1)
cls = pd.DataFrame(te.X.toarray(), columns=te.var_names).T.groupby(te.var["class"].values).sum().T
cls_share = cls.groupby(te.obs.stage.values).sum().div(cls.groupby(te.obs.stage.values).sum().sum(1), axis=0).mul(100).round(1).reindex(STAGES)
load.to_csv(qc / "irescue_te_load_by_stage.csv"); cls_share.to_csv(qc / "irescue_class_share_by_stage.csv")
pd.set_option("display.width", 250)
print("TE load by stage (medians per cell):\n", load.to_string())
print("share of TE UMIs by class (%):\n", cls_share[[c for c in ["SINE", "LINE", "LTR", "DNA", "Retroposon", "RC"] if c in cls_share]].to_string(), flush=True)


def pseudobulk_cpm(by):
    """TE UMIs per million gene UMIs, summed per group."""
    g = te.obs[by].values
    cnt = pd.DataFrame(te.X.toarray(), columns=te.var_names).groupby(g).sum()
    lib = te.obs.groupby(by)["gene_umis"].sum()
    return cnt.div(lib.reindex(cnt.index), axis=0) * 1e6


cpm_stage = pseudobulk_cpm("stage").reindex(STAGES)
cpm_group = pseudobulk_cpm("ATAC_WNN_annotation")
cpm_group = cpm_group.reindex([g for g in GROUP_ORDER if g in cpm_group.index])
cpm_stage.T.to_csv(qc / "irescue_cpm_by_stage.csv"); cpm_group.T.to_csv(qc / "irescue_cpm_by_group.csv")
focus = [f for f in FOCUS if f in cpm_stage.columns]
print("selected young / pluripotency-linked elements, UMIs per million gene UMIs, by stage:\n",
      cpm_stage[focus].T.round(1).to_string(), flush=True)

# ---- plots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(15, 4.5))
ax = axes[0]
data = [te.obs.loc[te.obs.stage == s, "te_per_10k_gene"].dropna().values for s in STAGES]
ax.boxplot(data, showfliers=False); ax.set_xticks(range(1, 9), STAGES); ax.set_ylabel("TE UMIs per 10k gene UMIs")
ax.set_title("TE load per cell by stage (IRescue, all TE classes)")
ax = axes[1]
for f in ["HERVH-int", "LTR7", "HERVK-int", "LTR5_Hs", "L1HS", "SVA_F"]:
    if f in cpm_stage:
        ax.plot(STAGES, cpm_stage[f].values, marker="o", label=f)
ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.set_ylabel("UMIs per million gene UMIs (pseudobulk)"); ax.legend(fontsize=9, frameon=False)
ax.set_title("Young elements across stages")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(qc / "irescue_stage_overview.png", dpi=100, bbox_inches="tight"); plt.close(fig)

# heatmap: most variable ERV (LTR-class) subfamilies across groups, among expressed ones
ltr = te.var_names[(te.var["class"] == "LTR").values]
sub = cpm_group[ltr]
sub = sub.loc[:, sub.max() >= 5]                       # at least 5 UMIs per million gene UMIs in some group
lg = np.log2(sub + 1)
top = lg.var().sort_values(ascending=False).index[:60]
z = (lg[top] - lg[top].mean()) / lg[top].std()
order = z.T.idxmax(axis=1).map({g: i for i, g in enumerate(z.index)}).sort_values().index  # sort by peak group
z = z[order]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 15))
im = ax.imshow(z.T.values, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-2.5, vmax=2.5, aspect="auto")
ax.set_xticks(range(len(z.index)), z.index, rotation=60, ha="right", fontsize=9)
ax.set_yticks(range(len(order)), [f"{o} ({te.var.loc[o, 'family']})" for o in order], fontsize=8)
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.025, label="z-score of log2(UMIs per million gene UMIs + 1)")
ax.set_title("60 most variable expressed ERV / LTR subfamilies across annotation groups (IRescue pseudobulk)")
fig.savefig(qc / "irescue_ERV_heatmap_by_group.png", dpi=80, bbox_inches="tight"); plt.close(fig)
z.T.round(3).to_csv(qc / "irescue_ERV_heatmap_values.csv")
peak = z.idxmax().rename("peak_group")
print("top variable ERV subfamilies and the group where each peaks:\n",
      pd.concat([peak, sub[order].max().round(1).rename("max_cpm")], axis=1).to_string(), flush=True)
print("done", qc, flush=True)

4.7 Pseudobulk (sample × cell group)

What
Sums counts over all cells of one cell group in one sample, giving one "unit". Units with fewer than 20 cells are dropped, leaving 119 units for each modality.
Why
Single-cell TE counts are very sparse. Testing on single cells treats cells as independent replicates and inflates significance. Pseudobulks summed per sample behave like bulk RNA-seq, which DESeq2 models well.
How
A sparse indicator matrix (units × cells) is multiplied by the count matrix. The unit library size is the sum of gene UMIs (RNA) or of all cut sites (ATAC). It also merges the ATAC per-cell tables into atac_te_subfamily_merged.h5ad.
scripts/07_pseudobulk_te.py
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
Pseudobulk TE-subfamily counts for DESeq2, for RNA (IRescue) and ATAC (fragment cut sites).

RNA : $TE_OUT/irescue_subfamily/irescue_subfamily_merged.h5ad (from 06_merge_irescue.py)
ATAC: $TE_OUT/atac_te_subfamily/<sample>.counts.tsv.gz and .cell_totals.tsv (from 05_atac_te_counts.sb)
Cells: include_downstream == True. Units: sample x ATAC_WNN_annotation group with >= --min-cells cells.
Library size per unit (used as DESeq2 size factors): RNA = summed gene UMIs; ATAC = summed cut sites.

Outputs ($TE_OUT/deseq2/{rna,atac}/): counts.csv (subfamilies x units), coldata.csv
  (unit, sample, stage, diff_batch, group, n_cells, lib_size), subfamily_info.csv (family, class).
Also merges the ATAC per-cell counts into $TE_OUT/atac_te_subfamily/atac_te_subfamily_merged.h5ad.
"""
import argparse
import os
from pathlib import Path

import anndata as ad
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import scipy.sparse as sp

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TE_OUT = Path(os.environ["TE_OUT"]); ANNOT = Path(os.environ["ANNOTATION_CSV"])
TE_ANNOT = Path(os.environ["TE_ANNOT_DIR"])
ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--min-cells", type=int, default=20)
args = ap.parse_args()

samples = pd.read_csv(REPO / "configs/samples.tsv", sep="\t")["sample"].tolist()
ann = pd.read_csv(ANNOT, index_col=0, dtype=str)
keep = ann.index[ann.include_downstream.str.lower() == "true"]
rm = pd.read_csv(TE_ANNOT / "rmsk_hg38.bed.gz", sep="\t", header=None, usecols=[3, 6, 7],
                 names=["subfamily", "family", "class"]).drop_duplicates("subfamily").set_index("subfamily")
rm["class"] = rm["class"].str.rstrip("?")

# ---- ATAC: merge per-sample long tables into cells x subfamilies
parts, tot = [], []
for s in samples:
    d = TE_OUT / "atac_te_subfamily"
    c = pd.read_csv(d / f"{s}.counts.tsv.gz", sep="\t", header=None, names=["barcode", "subfamily", "n"])
    c["cell"] = s + "#" + c.barcode
    parts.append(c[["cell", "subfamily", "n"]])
    t = pd.read_csv(d / f"{s}.cell_totals.tsv", sep="\t"); t.index = s + "#" + t.barcode
    tot.append(t[["total_cut_sites", "te_cut_sites"]])
long = pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True)
tot = pd.concat(tot)
cells = pd.Index(tot.index.intersection(keep))
subs = pd.Index(sorted(long.subfamily.unique()))
long = long[long.cell.isin(cells)]
X = sp.csr_matrix((long.n.values.astype(np.float32), (cells.get_indexer(long.cell), subs.get_indexer(long.subfamily))),
                  shape=(len(cells), len(subs)))
atac = ad.AnnData(X=X, obs=ann.loc[cells, ["stage", "ATAC_WNN_annotation"]].join(tot), var=pd.DataFrame(index=subs))
atac.var = atac.var.join(rm)
atac.write_h5ad(TE_OUT / "atac_te_subfamily" / "atac_te_subfamily_merged.h5ad", compression="gzip")
print(f"ATAC merged: {atac.n_obs} cells x {atac.n_vars} subfamilies; "
      f"TE share of cut sites {100 * atac.obs.te_cut_sites.sum() / atac.obs.total_cut_sites.sum():.1f}%", flush=True)

# ---- RNA
rna = ad.read_h5ad(TE_OUT / "irescue_subfamily" / "irescue_subfamily_merged.h5ad")
rna = rna[rna.obs_names.isin(keep)].copy()


def pseudobulk(a, lib_col, outdir):
    outdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    o = a.obs.copy()
    o["sample"] = [n.split("#")[0] for n in a.obs_names]
    o["unit"] = o["sample"] + "__" + o["ATAC_WNN_annotation"].astype(str)
    n = o["unit"].value_counts()
    units = n.index[n >= args.min_cells].sort_values()
    codes = pd.Categorical(o["unit"], categories=units).codes
    m = codes >= 0
    ind = sp.csr_matrix((np.ones(m.sum()), (codes[m], np.where(m)[0])), shape=(len(units), a.n_obs))
    cnt = pd.DataFrame(np.rint((ind @ a.X).toarray()).astype(np.int64).T, index=a.var_names, columns=units)
    cd = pd.DataFrame(index=units)
    cd["sample"] = [u.split("__")[0] for u in units]
    cd["group"] = [u.split("__")[1] for u in units]
    cd["stage"] = [s.split("_")[1] for s in cd["sample"]]
    cd["diff_batch"] = [s.split("_")[0] for s in cd["sample"]]
    cd["n_cells"] = n.reindex(units).values
    cd["lib_size"] = o.groupby("unit")[lib_col].sum().reindex(units).values
    cd.index.name = "unit"
    cnt.to_csv(outdir / "counts.csv"); cd.to_csv(outdir / "coldata.csv")
    info = pd.DataFrame(index=a.var_names).join(rm); info.to_csv(outdir / "subfamily_info.csv")
    print(f"{outdir.name}: {cnt.shape[0]} subfamilies x {cnt.shape[1]} units "
          f"({cd.group.nunique()} groups; dropped {(n < args.min_cells).sum()} units under {args.min_cells} cells)", flush=True)
    return cd


cd_rna = pseudobulk(rna, "gene_umis", TE_OUT / "deseq2" / "rna")
cd_atac = pseudobulk(atac, "total_cut_sites", TE_OUT / "deseq2" / "atac")
print(cd_rna.groupby("group").size().to_string())

4.8 Differential testing with DESeq2

What
For each modality, two marker-style tests: each cell group vs the mean of all other groups, and each stage vs the mean of all other stages. For the stage test, units are summed per sample. A call means padj < 0.05 and log2FC > 1. Subfamilies with a mean count below 10 are dropped.
Why DESeq2
It models counts as negative binomial and shares dispersion information across subfamilies, which stabilises estimates with few replicates. It also shrinks noisy fold changes toward zero.
How
The model is ~ 0 + group, so each group gets its own coefficient (its mean log expression). The "group g vs rest" contrast uses weight +1 for g and −1/(k−1) for each of the other k−1 groups. This tests g against the average of the others on the log scale, a balanced comparison that is not driven by one big group.
Size factors are fixed to each unit's library size (gene UMIs or total cut sites), scaled to a geometric mean of 1. DESeq2's usual median-of-ratios on the TE counts would be dominated by old intronic SINEs and LINEs, which change with nuclear RNA content rather than with sequencing depth.
No sample term. hPSC exists only at D0 and DE mostly at D4, so a sample term would absorb those group effects (see §2).
scripts/08_deseq2_te.R
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# Pseudobulk DESeq2 for TE subfamilies (input from 07_pseudobulk_te.py), one modality per call.
#
# Units are sample x ATAC_WNN_annotation group. In the early stages each group comes from one sample
# (hPSC only from D0, DE only from D4), so blocking on sample would remove the stage/cell-type
# contrasts this project asks about. Design is therefore ~ group, with the sample x group pseudobulks
# as replicates; stage and differentiation batch stay confounded (only D7/D9 have two batches).
#
# Size factors come from each unit's library size (RNA: gene UMIs; ATAC: all cut sites), scaled to a
# geometric mean of 1 -- not from the TE counts, which are dominated by old intronic repeats.
#
#   groups: each group vs the mean of all other groups (marker-style contrast)
#   stages: units summed per sample, ~ stage, each stage vs the mean of the other stages
# Calls: padj < 0.05 and log2FC > 1; subfamilies with mean count < 10 dropped.
# Usage: Rscript 08_deseq2_te.R <deseq2 dir for one modality: counts.csv, coldata.csv, subfamily_info.csv>

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(DESeq2))
args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
d <- args[1]
out <- file.path(d, "results"); dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)
counts <- as.matrix(read.csv(file.path(d, "counts.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
cd <- read.csv(file.path(d, "coldata.csv"), row.names = 1, stringsAsFactors = TRUE)[colnames(counts), ]
info <- read.csv(file.path(d, "subfamily_info.csv"), row.names = 1)
counts <- counts[rowMeans(counts) >= 10, ]
cat(sprintf("%s: %d subfamilies, %d units, %d groups\n", basename(d), nrow(counts), ncol(counts), nlevels(cd$group)))

vs_rest <- function(dds, factor_name, levels_, tag) {
  rn <- resultsNames(dds)
  res_all <- list()
  for (g in levels_) {
    w <- setNames(rep(-1 / (length(levels_) - 1), length(levels_)), paste0(factor_name, levels_))
    w[paste0(factor_name, g)] <- 1
    v <- setNames(rep(0, length(rn)), rn); v[names(w)] <- w
    r <- as.data.frame(results(dds, contrast = v))
    r$subfamily <- rownames(r); r$family <- info[r$subfamily, "family"]; r$class <- info[r$subfamily, "class"]
    r$level <- g
    res_all[[g]] <- r
  }
  all <- do.call(rbind, res_all)
  write.csv(all, file.path(out, sprintf("%s_vs_rest_all.csv", tag)), row.names = FALSE)
  up <- all[!is.na(all$padj) & all$padj < 0.05 & all$log2FoldChange > 1, ]
  up <- up[order(up$level, -up$log2FoldChange), ]
  write.csv(up, file.path(out, sprintf("%s_vs_rest_up.csv", tag)), row.names = FALSE)
  erv <- up[up$class == "LTR", ]
  cat(sprintf("\n== %s: subfamilies up vs rest (padj<0.05, log2FC>1): %d total, %d ERV/LTR\n", tag, nrow(up), nrow(erv)))
  for (g in levels_) {
    e <- erv[erv$level == g, ]
    e <- e[e$baseMean > 20, ]
    if (nrow(e)) cat(sprintf("  %s (%d): %s\n", g, nrow(e),
      paste(sprintf("%s %.1f", head(e$subfamily, 12), head(e$log2FoldChange, 12)), collapse = ", ")))
  }
  invisible(all)
}

sf <- function(lib) { s <- lib / exp(mean(log(lib))); s }

# groups
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(counts, cd, ~ 0 + group)
sizeFactors(dds) <- sf(cd$lib_size)
dds <- DESeq(dds, quiet = TRUE)
vs_rest(dds, "group", levels(cd$group), "group")
saveRDS(dds, file.path(out, "dds_group.rds"))

# stages (sum units per sample)
smp <- factor(cd$sample)
sc <- sapply(levels(smp), function(s) rowSums(counts[, smp == s, drop = FALSE]))
scd <- data.frame(row.names = levels(smp), stage = factor(sapply(strsplit(levels(smp), "_"), `[`, 2),
                  levels = c("D0", "D4", "D7", "D9", "D12", "D15", "D22", "D45")),
                  lib_size = tapply(cd$lib_size, smp, sum)[levels(smp)])
scd$stage <- droplevels(scd$stage)
dds2 <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(sc, scd, ~ 0 + stage)
sizeFactors(dds2) <- sf(scd$lib_size)
dds2 <- DESeq(dds2, quiet = TRUE)
vs_rest(dds2, "stage", levels(scd$stage), "stage")
norm <- counts(dds2, normalized = TRUE)
write.csv(round(norm, 2), file.path(out, "stage_normalized_counts.csv"))
cat("\ndone:", out, "\n")

4.9 scTE merge and pseudobulk (same units as IRescue)

What
Merges scTE outputs for each mode. It separates TE columns from gene columns using the TE BED's subfamily names and pseudobulks into exactly the 119 IRescue units. DESeq2 (4.8) then runs on both modes.
Why
Using identical units and normalisation means any difference between IRescue, exclusive and nointron results comes from the counting, not from the statistics.
How / checks
scTE kept every whitelisted cell except 6 in D7_rep2. TE columns hold 50–78% of all scTE counts in exclusive mode but only ~10% in nointron mode. This alone shows how much of the TE signal in nuclei comes from introns.
Gotcha
config.sh does not export its variables, so Python jobs need set -a; source config.sh; set +a.
scripts/10_merge_scte.py
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
Merge the scTE RNA outputs (exclusive and nointron indexes) and pseudobulk them like the IRescue counts.

scTE writes genes and TE subfamilies into one cells x features matrix; TE columns are the subfamily
names of the scTE TE BED ($TE_ANNOT_DIR/scte/hg38_TE.bed). The two indexes differ in where a read on
a TE is kept as a TE read:
  exclusive : TE reads on exons of genes go to the gene; intronic and intergenic TE reads count as TE
  nointron  : TE reads anywhere in a gene body go to the gene; only intergenic TE reads count as TE
so nointron / exclusive per subfamily = share of its TE signal from copies outside genes. A subfamily
whose induction rests on intronic copies (host-gene pre-mRNA, common in single-nucleus RNA) loses it
in nointron.

Inputs : $TE_OUT/scte_rna_{exclusive,nointron}/<sample>.h5ad (04_scte_rna.sb)
         shared annotation (include_downstream == True cells only) and per-cell gene UMIs
Outputs: $TE_OUT/scte_rna_<mode>/scte_<mode>_merged.h5ad       (kept cells x TE subfamilies)
         $TE_OUT/deseq2/scte_<mode>/{counts,coldata,subfamily_info}.csv
             same units as $TE_OUT/deseq2/rna (IRescue); lib_size = gene UMIs of the cells scTE kept
         $TE_OUT/qc/scte_mode_totals.csv          per subfamily: IRescue / exclusive / nointron totals
         $TE_OUT/qc/scte_intergenic_fraction_by_group.csv   nointron / exclusive per subfamily x group
"""
import os
from pathlib import Path

import anndata as ad
import h5py
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import scipy.sparse as sp

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TE_OUT = Path(os.environ["TE_OUT"]); ANNOT = Path(os.environ["ANNOTATION_CSV"])
SCP_OUT = Path(os.environ["SCP_OUT"]); TE_ANNOT = Path(os.environ["TE_ANNOT_DIR"])
MODES = ["exclusive", "nointron"]
qc = TE_OUT / "qc"; qc.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

samples = pd.read_csv(REPO / "configs/samples.tsv", sep="\t")["sample"].tolist()
ann = pd.read_csv(ANNOT, index_col=0, dtype=str)
ann = ann[ann.include_downstream.str.lower() == "true"]
te_names = set(pd.read_csv(TE_ANNOT / "scte/hg38_TE.bed", sep="\t", header=None, usecols=[3])[3].unique())
rm = pd.read_csv(TE_ANNOT / "rmsk_hg38.bed.gz", sep="\t", header=None, usecols=[3, 6, 7],
                 names=["subfamily", "family", "class"]).drop_duplicates("subfamily").set_index("subfamily")
rm["class"] = rm["class"].str.rstrip("?")
with h5py.File(SCP_OUT / "integration/h5ad/merged_rna_scvi_integrated.h5ad", "r") as h:
    gene_umis = pd.Series(h["obs"]["total_counts"][:], index=h["obs"]["_index"][:].astype(str))
units_ref = pd.read_csv(TE_OUT / "deseq2/rna/coldata.csv", index_col=0)   # IRescue units


def merge(mode):
    blocks, names, gcounts, subs = [], [], [], None
    for s in samples:
        a = ad.read_h5ad(TE_OUT / f"scte_rna_{mode}" / f"{s}.h5ad")
        a.obs_names = s + "#" + a.obs_names.astype(str)
        a = a[a.obs_names.isin(ann.index)]
        is_te = a.var_names.isin(te_names)
        if subs is None:
            subs = a.var_names[is_te]
        X = a.X.tocsr()
        gcounts.append(np.asarray(X[:, ~is_te].sum(1)).ravel())
        blocks.append(X[:, a.var_names.get_indexer(subs)])
        names += list(a.obs_names)
        n_ann = ann.index.str.startswith(s + "#").sum()
        print(f"{mode} {s}: {a.n_obs}/{n_ann} kept cells in scTE output, {is_te.sum()} TE columns, "
              f"TE share of counts {100 * blocks[-1].sum() / X.sum():.1f}%", flush=True)
    te = ad.AnnData(X=sp.vstack(blocks).tocsr().astype(np.float32), var=pd.DataFrame(index=subs))
    te.obs_names = names
    te.obs = ann.loc[names, ["stage", "ATAC_WNN_annotation"]].copy()
    te.obs["sample"] = [n.split("#")[0] for n in names]
    te.obs["scte_gene_counts"] = np.concatenate(gcounts)
    te.obs["gene_umis"] = gene_umis.reindex(names).values
    te.var = te.var.join(rm)
    te.write_h5ad(TE_OUT / f"scte_rna_{mode}" / f"scte_{mode}_merged.h5ad", compression="gzip")
    return te


def pseudobulk(te, mode):
    o = te.obs
    unit = (o["sample"].astype(str) + "__" + o["ATAC_WNN_annotation"].astype(str)).values
    units = units_ref.index
    codes = pd.Categorical(unit, categories=units).codes
    m = codes >= 0
    ind = sp.csr_matrix((np.ones(m.sum()), (codes[m], np.where(m)[0])), shape=(len(units), te.n_obs))
    cnt = pd.DataFrame(np.rint((ind @ te.X).toarray()).astype(np.int64).T, index=te.var_names, columns=units)
    cd = units_ref.copy()
    cd["n_cells"] = pd.Series(unit).value_counts().reindex(units).fillna(0).astype(int).values
    cd["lib_size"] = pd.Series(o["gene_umis"].values, index=unit).groupby(level=0).sum().reindex(units).values
    out = TE_OUT / "deseq2" / f"scte_{mode}"; out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    cnt.to_csv(out / "counts.csv"); cd.to_csv(out / "coldata.csv")
    te.var[["family", "class"]].to_csv(out / "subfamily_info.csv")
    lost = (cd.n_cells / units_ref.n_cells)
    print(f"{mode}: {cnt.shape[0]} subfamilies x {cnt.shape[1]} units; cells kept per unit vs IRescue: "
          f"median {lost.median():.3f}, min {lost.min():.3f} ({lost.idxmin()})", flush=True)
    return cnt


cnts = {m: pseudobulk(merge(m), m) for m in MODES}
ir = pd.read_csv(TE_OUT / "deseq2/rna/counts.csv", index_col=0)
grp = units_ref["group"]

tot = pd.DataFrame({"irescue": ir.sum(1), "exclusive": cnts["exclusive"].sum(1), "nointron": cnts["nointron"].sum(1)})
tot = tot.join(rm)
tot["intergenic_frac"] = tot.nointron / tot.exclusive
tot["exclusive_vs_irescue"] = tot.exclusive / tot.irescue
tot.sort_values("exclusive", ascending=False).to_csv(qc / "scte_mode_totals.csv")
by_grp = {m: cnts[m].T.groupby(grp.reindex(cnts[m].columns).values).sum().T for m in MODES}
frac = (by_grp["nointron"] / by_grp["exclusive"].where(by_grp["exclusive"] >= 20)).round(3)
frac.to_csv(qc / "scte_intergenic_fraction_by_group.csv")

pd.set_option("display.width", 250)
s = tot.groupby("class")[["irescue", "exclusive", "nointron"]].sum()
s["intergenic_frac"] = s.nointron / s.exclusive
print("totals by class:\n", s.sort_values("exclusive", ascending=False).head(8).round(3).to_string())
focus = ["HERVH-int", "LTR7", "HERVS71-int", "HERV15-int", "LTR12_", "LTR12E", "MLT1F2", "LTR48B", "MER92-int",
         "MER110-int", "HERVK11-int", "HERVK-int", "HERVE-int", "HERV4_I-int", "HERVIP10B3-int", "HERVI-int", "PABL_A-int"]
print("focus subfamilies:\n", tot.reindex([f for f in focus if f in tot.index])
      [["family", "irescue", "exclusive", "nointron", "intergenic_frac", "exclusive_vs_irescue"]].round(3).to_string())
print("done", flush=True)

4.10 Read-through check: exclusive vs nointron

What
Gives every group-vs-rest or stage-vs-rest call from IRescue or scTE-exclusive a verdict on whether it is supported by copies outside genes.
Logic
If a subfamily is "induced" only because a host gene containing some of its copies is switched on, the extra reads land in introns. They are present in exclusive mode and vanish in nointron mode. If the subfamily's own LTRs drive transcription at copies outside genes, the induction persists in nointron.
Verdicts
intergenic also up in nointron (padj < 0.05, log2FC > 1) · weak nointron log2FC > 0.5 but not called · no_intergenic too few reads outside genes to test · intronic_only nointron log2FC ≤ 0.5, a read-through suspect
Extra metric
frac_ratio = (nointron ÷ exclusive in the called group) ÷ (same ratio in all other groups). Below 1, the group's extra TE reads come mostly from copies inside genes. Above 1, they come mostly from copies outside genes.
scripts/11_compare_scte_modes.py
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
Flag host-gene read-through among the TE calls: compare IRescue, scTE exclusive and scTE nointron.

For each subfamily x level (group or stage) called up vs rest (padj < 0.05, log2FC > 1) by IRescue or
scTE exclusive, ask whether the induction survives when only intergenic TE reads count (nointron):
  intergenic      nointron also up (padj < 0.05, log2FC > 1)
  weak            nointron log2FC > 0.5 but not called
  no_intergenic   nointron mean count < 10 (filtered) -- almost all signal is in genes
  intronic_only   nointron log2FC <= 0.5 -- induction carried by copies inside genes (read-through suspect)
Also: frac_level / frac_rest = nointron / exclusive counts in that level vs all other levels; a low
ratio means the induced level's TE reads come disproportionately from genic copies.

Inputs : $TE_OUT/deseq2/{rna,scte_exclusive,scte_nointron}/results/<tag>_vs_rest_all.csv, counts.csv, coldata.csv
Outputs: $TE_OUT/qc/scte_mode_comparison_{group,stage}.csv, scte_mode_lfc_scatter.png
"""
import os
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

TE_OUT = Path(os.environ["TE_OUT"]); D = TE_OUT / "deseq2"; qc = TE_OUT / "qc"
MODES = {"ir": "rna", "ex": "scte_exclusive", "no": "scte_nointron"}
FOCUS = ["HERVS71-int", "HERV15-int", "LTR12_", "LTR12E", "MLT1F2", "LTR48B", "MER92-int", "MER110-int"]
pd.set_option("display.width", 250); pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 400)


def level_counts(mode, tag):
    cnt = pd.read_csv(D / mode / "counts.csv", index_col=0)
    cd = pd.read_csv(D / mode / "coldata.csv", index_col=0).reindex(cnt.columns)
    return cnt.T.groupby(cd[tag].values).sum().T


def compare(tag):
    res = {}
    for k, m in MODES.items():
        r = pd.read_csv(D / m / "results" / f"{tag}_vs_rest_all.csv").set_index(["subfamily", "level"])
        res[k] = r[["baseMean", "log2FoldChange", "padj"]].add_suffix(f"_{k}")
        if k == "ex":
            fam = r[["family", "class"]]
    t = res["ex"].join(res["no"], how="left").join(res["ir"], how="outer").join(fam, how="left")
    for k in MODES:
        t[f"up_{k}"] = (t[f"padj_{k}"] < 0.05) & (t[f"log2FoldChange_{k}"] > 1)
    t = t.reset_index()
    ex, no = level_counts(MODES["ex"], tag), level_counts(MODES["no"], tag)
    tot_ex, tot_no = ex.sum(1), no.sum(1)
    t["frac_overall"] = (tot_no / tot_ex).reindex(t.subfamily).values
    lv_ex = ex.stack().reindex(list(zip(t.subfamily, t.level))).values
    lv_no = no.stack().reindex(list(zip(t.subfamily, t.level))).values
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        t["frac_level"] = lv_no / lv_ex
    t["frac_rest"] = (tot_no.reindex(t.subfamily).values - lv_no) / (tot_ex.reindex(t.subfamily).values - lv_ex)
    t["frac_ratio"] = t.frac_level / t.frac_rest
    called = t.up_ir | t.up_ex
    v = np.select([t.up_no, t.log2FoldChange_no > 0.5, t.log2FoldChange_no.isna()],
                  ["intergenic", "weak", "no_intergenic"], "intronic_only")
    t["verdict"] = np.where(called, v, "")
    t = t.sort_values(["level", "log2FoldChange_ex"], ascending=[True, False])
    t.round(4).to_csv(qc / f"scte_mode_comparison_{tag}.csv", index=False)

    print(f"\n===== {tag}: up vs rest in IRescue / exclusive / nointron: "
          f"{t.up_ir.sum()} / {t.up_ex.sum()} / {t.up_no.sum()}  (all classes)")
    c = t[t.verdict != ""]
    print("verdicts for calls (IRescue or exclusive), by class:\n",
          pd.crosstab(c["class"], c.verdict).loc[lambda x: x.sum(1) >= 3].to_string())
    print("agreement IRescue vs exclusive among calls:", pd.crosstab(c.up_ir, c.up_ex).to_string().replace("\n", " | "))
    ok = t.baseMean_ex.gt(20) & t.baseMean_ir.gt(20)
    print(f"log2FC correlation (baseMean > 20 in both): IRescue~exclusive r={t[ok].log2FoldChange_ir.corr(t[ok].log2FoldChange_ex):.2f}; "
          f"exclusive~nointron r={t[ok].log2FoldChange_ex.corr(t[ok].log2FoldChange_no):.2f}")
    cols = ["subfamily", "level", "family", "baseMean_ir", "log2FoldChange_ir", "log2FoldChange_ex", "log2FoldChange_no",
            "padj_no", "frac_overall", "frac_level", "frac_ratio", "verdict"]
    erv = c[(c["class"] == "LTR") & (c.baseMean_ex > 20)]
    print(f"ERV/LTR calls with baseMean_ex > 20 ({len(erv)}):")
    print(erv[cols].round(2).to_string(index=False))
    f = t[t.subfamily.isin(FOCUS) & ((t.verdict != "") | t.up_no)]
    print("focus subfamilies:\n", f[cols].round(2).to_string(index=False), flush=True)
    return t


g = compare("group")
s = compare("stage")

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.5))
col = {"intergenic": "#1b7837", "weak": "#a6dba0", "no_intergenic": "#999999", "intronic_only": "#c51b7d"}
for ax, (x, y, ttl) in zip(axes, [("log2FoldChange_ir", "log2FoldChange_ex", "IRescue vs scTE exclusive"),
                                  ("log2FoldChange_ex", "log2FoldChange_no", "scTE exclusive vs nointron")]):
    d = g[(g["class"] == "LTR") & (g.baseMean_ex > 20)]
    ax.scatter(d[x], d[y], s=4, c="#dddddd", rasterized=True)
    for vv, cc in col.items():
        e = d[d.verdict == vv]
        ax.scatter(e[x], e[y], s=10, c=cc, label=f"{vv} ({len(e)})")
    ax.axhline(0, c="k", lw=0.5); ax.axvline(0, c="k", lw=0.5); ax.plot([-8, 8], [-8, 8], c="k", lw=0.5, ls="--")
    ax.set_xlabel(x); ax.set_ylabel(y); ax.set_title(f"ERV/LTR subfamily x group vs rest: {ttl}")
axes[1].legend(fontsize=8, frameon=False, title="verdict (calls)")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(qc / "scte_mode_lfc_scatter.png", dpi=100, bbox_inches="tight")
print("done", qc)

4.11 ATAC method comparison (cut sites vs scTEATAC)

What
scTEATAC counts are pseudobulked into the same 119 units, with the same size factors (total cut sites). DESeq2 then runs exactly as for cut sites, and fold changes and calls are compared.
Why
To see whether the missing low-MAPQ reads cost us ERV calls (young, repetitive families), and whether counting fragment spans rather than cut sites changes anything.
scripts/12_merge_scte_atac.py
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
Merge the scTEATAC outputs (05b_scte_atac.sb) and pseudobulk them into the ATAC units of 07, so DESeq2
(08) runs on exactly the same units and size factors (total cut sites from 05) as the cut-site counts.

Inputs : $TE_OUT/scte_atac/<sample>.h5ad (cells x TE subfamilies; fragments overlapping each subfamily)
         $TE_OUT/deseq2/atac/coldata.csv (units, lib_size), shared annotation, cell totals from 05
Outputs: $TE_OUT/scte_atac/scte_atac_merged.h5ad
         $TE_OUT/deseq2/scte_atac/{counts,coldata,subfamily_info}.csv
"""
import os
from pathlib import Path

import anndata as ad
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import scipy.sparse as sp

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TE_OUT = Path(os.environ["TE_OUT"]); ANNOT = Path(os.environ["ANNOTATION_CSV"])
TE_ANNOT = Path(os.environ["TE_ANNOT_DIR"])

samples = pd.read_csv(REPO / "configs/samples.tsv", sep="\t")["sample"].tolist()
ann = pd.read_csv(ANNOT, index_col=0, dtype=str)
ann = ann[ann.include_downstream.str.lower() == "true"]
rm = pd.read_csv(TE_ANNOT / "rmsk_hg38.bed.gz", sep="\t", header=None, usecols=[3, 6, 7],
                 names=["subfamily", "family", "class"]).drop_duplicates("subfamily").set_index("subfamily")
rm["class"] = rm["class"].str.rstrip("?")
units_ref = pd.read_csv(TE_OUT / "deseq2/atac/coldata.csv", index_col=0)

blocks, names, subs = [], [], None
for s in samples:
    a = ad.read_h5ad(TE_OUT / "scte_atac" / f"{s}.h5ad")
    a.obs_names = s + "#" + a.obs_names.astype(str)
    a = a[a.obs_names.isin(ann.index)]
    if subs is None:
        subs = a.var_names
    blocks.append(sp.csr_matrix(a.X)[:, a.var_names.get_indexer(subs)])
    names += list(a.obs_names)
    tot = pd.read_csv(TE_OUT / "atac_te_subfamily" / f"{s}.cell_totals.tsv", sep="\t")
    print(f"{s}: {a.n_obs}/{ann.index.str.startswith(s + '#').sum()} kept cells, "
          f"{blocks[-1].sum():,.0f} TE fragment hits vs {tot.te_cut_sites.sum():,} TE cut sites", flush=True)
te = ad.AnnData(X=sp.vstack(blocks).tocsr().astype(np.float32), var=pd.DataFrame(index=subs))
te.obs_names = names
te.obs = ann.loc[names, ["stage", "ATAC_WNN_annotation"]].copy()
te.obs["sample"] = [n.split("#")[0] for n in names]
te.var = te.var.join(rm)
te.write_h5ad(TE_OUT / "scte_atac" / "scte_atac_merged.h5ad", compression="gzip")

unit = (te.obs["sample"].astype(str) + "__" + te.obs["ATAC_WNN_annotation"].astype(str)).values
units = units_ref.index
codes = pd.Categorical(unit, categories=units).codes
m = codes >= 0
ind = sp.csr_matrix((np.ones(m.sum()), (codes[m], np.where(m)[0])), shape=(len(units), te.n_obs))
cnt = pd.DataFrame(np.rint((ind @ te.X).toarray()).astype(np.int64).T, index=te.var_names, columns=units)
cd = units_ref.copy()          # lib_size = total cut sites (05), as for the cut-site counts
n = pd.Series(unit).value_counts().reindex(units).fillna(0).astype(int)
assert (n.values == cd.n_cells.values).all(), "cells per unit differ from the cut-site units"
out = TE_OUT / "deseq2" / "scte_atac"; out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
cnt.to_csv(out / "counts.csv"); cd.to_csv(out / "coldata.csv")
te.var[["family", "class"]].to_csv(out / "subfamily_info.csv")
print(f"scte_atac: {cnt.shape[0]} subfamilies x {cnt.shape[1]} units", flush=True)
scripts/13_compare_atac_methods.py
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
Compare ATAC TE-subfamily results from cut sites in fragments (05, MAPQ >= 30 only) and scTEATAC
(05b, fragment spans, all MAPQ incl. multi-mapping reads), on identical units and size factors.

  1. totals per subfamily: scTEATAC / cut-site ratio; a high ratio = signal recovered from
     multi-mapping reads (young, repetitive families)
  2. DESeq2 group / stage vs rest: log2FC correlation, call overlap (padj < 0.05, log2FC > 1)
  3. per call, agreement: both / cut_only / scte_only; the young families listed explicitly

Inputs : $TE_OUT/deseq2/{atac,scte_atac}/counts.csv and results/<tag>_vs_rest_all.csv
Outputs: $TE_OUT/qc/atac_method_totals.csv, atac_method_comparison_{group,stage}.csv, atac_method_scatter.png
"""
import os
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

TE_OUT = Path(os.environ["TE_OUT"]); D = TE_OUT / "deseq2"; qc = TE_OUT / "qc"
YOUNG = ["LTR5_Hs", "HERVK-int", "LTR7", "LTR7Y", "HERVH-int", "LTR12C", "LTR12_", "L1HS", "L1PA2", "L1PA3",
         "SVA_D", "SVA_E", "SVA_F", "AluY", "LTR6A", "LTR6B", "LTR22", "LTR22B", "LTR15", "LTR10D"]
pd.set_option("display.width", 250); pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 300)

cut = pd.read_csv(D / "atac/counts.csv", index_col=0).sum(1)
sct = pd.read_csv(D / "scte_atac/counts.csv", index_col=0).sum(1)
info = pd.read_csv(D / "atac/subfamily_info.csv", index_col=0)
tot = pd.concat([cut.rename("cut_sites"), sct.rename("scte_fragments")], axis=1).join(info)
tot["ratio"] = tot.scte_fragments / tot.cut_sites
tot.sort_values("ratio", ascending=False).to_csv(qc / "atac_method_totals.csv")
ok = tot[(tot.cut_sites > 1000) & (tot.scte_fragments > 0)]
print(f"per-subfamily totals: log10 r = {np.corrcoef(np.log10(ok.cut_sites), np.log10(ok.scte_fragments))[0, 1]:.3f}; "
      f"median scTEATAC/cut ratio {ok.ratio.median():.2f}")
print("highest ratios (gain from multi-mapping reads):\n",
      ok.sort_values("ratio", ascending=False).head(15)[["family", "class", "cut_sites", "scte_fragments", "ratio"]].round(2).to_string())
print("young / focus families:\n", tot.reindex([y for y in YOUNG if y in tot.index])[["family", "cut_sites", "scte_fragments", "ratio"]].round(2).to_string())


def compare(tag):
    r = {}
    for k, m in {"cut": "atac", "scte": "scte_atac"}.items():
        x = pd.read_csv(D / m / "results" / f"{tag}_vs_rest_all.csv").set_index(["subfamily", "level"])
        r[k] = x[["baseMean", "log2FoldChange", "padj"]].add_suffix(f"_{k}")
        if k == "cut":
            fam = x[["family", "class"]]
    t = r["cut"].join(r["scte"], how="outer").join(fam, how="left")
    for k in r:
        t[f"up_{k}"] = (t[f"padj_{k}"] < 0.05) & (t[f"log2FoldChange_{k}"] > 1)
    t["agreement"] = np.select([t.up_cut & t.up_scte, t.up_cut, t.up_scte], ["both", "cut_only", "scte_only"], "")
    t = t.reset_index().sort_values(["level", "log2FoldChange_cut"], ascending=[True, False])
    t.round(4).to_csv(qc / f"atac_method_comparison_{tag}.csv", index=False)
    b = t[(t.baseMean_cut > 20) & (t.baseMean_scte > 20)]
    print(f"\n===== {tag}: calls cut / scTEATAC / both = {t.up_cut.sum()} / {t.up_scte.sum()} / {(t.agreement == 'both').sum()}; "
          f"log2FC r = {b.log2FoldChange_cut.corr(b.log2FoldChange_scte):.2f} (baseMean > 20 in both)")
    c = t[t.agreement != ""]
    print("agreement by class:\n", pd.crosstab(c["class"], c.agreement).loc[lambda x: x.sum(1) >= 5].to_string())
    print("per level (LTR calls):\n", pd.crosstab(c[c["class"] == "LTR"].level, c[c["class"] == "LTR"].agreement).to_string())
    cols = ["subfamily", "level", "log2FoldChange_cut", "padj_cut", "log2FoldChange_scte", "padj_scte", "agreement"]
    one = c[(c["class"] == "LTR") & (c.agreement != "both") & (c[["baseMean_cut", "baseMean_scte"]].max(1) > 50)]
    print(f"LTR calls found by one method only (baseMean > 50): {len(one)}")
    print(one.sort_values(["agreement", "level"])[cols].round(2).head(60).to_string(index=False))
    y = t[t.subfamily.isin(YOUNG) & (t.up_cut | t.up_scte)]
    print("young / focus families, any call:\n", y[cols].round(2).to_string(index=False), flush=True)
    return t


g = compare("group")
compare("stage")

d = g[(g["class"] == "LTR") & (g.baseMean_cut > 20)]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 6))
ax.scatter(d.log2FoldChange_cut, d.log2FoldChange_scte, s=4, c="#cccccc", rasterized=True)
for a, col in {"both": "#1b7837", "cut_only": "#2166ac", "scte_only": "#b2182b"}.items():
    e = d[d.agreement == a]
    ax.scatter(e.log2FoldChange_cut, e.log2FoldChange_scte, s=9, c=col, label=f"{a} ({len(e)})")
lim = np.nanmax(np.abs(d[["log2FoldChange_cut", "log2FoldChange_scte"]].values)) * 1.05
ax.plot([-lim, lim], [-lim, lim], c="k", lw=0.5, ls="--"); ax.axhline(0, c="k", lw=0.5); ax.axvline(0, c="k", lw=0.5)
ax.set_xlabel("log2FC, cut sites (fragments, MAPQ >= 30)"); ax.set_ylabel("log2FC, scTEATAC (fragment spans, all MAPQ)")
ax.set_title("ATAC: ERV/LTR subfamily x group vs rest"); ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(qc / "atac_method_scatter.png", dpi=110)
print("done", qc)
scripts/12_scte_atac_deseq2.sb
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4
#SBATCH --mem=64G
#SBATCH --time=02:00:00
