#SBATCH --output=logs/scte_atac_de.%j.out
# After 05b: merge + pseudobulk scTEATAC (12), DESeq2 (08), compare with the cut-site ATAC results (13).
# Usage: sbatch scripts/12_scte_atac_deseq2.sb
set -euo pipefail
set -a; source config.sh; set +a
"$TE_ENV/bin/python" scripts/12_merge_scte_atac.py
"$R_ENV/bin/Rscript" scripts/08_deseq2_te.R "$TE_OUT/deseq2/scte_atac" 2>&1 | grep -v R_HOME
"$TE_ENV/bin/python" scripts/13_compare_atac_methods.py

4.12 Candidate tiers (all methods on equal footing)

Why
Choosing either RNA method as the "main" one and applying a hard cutoff loses candidates. Of the group calls supported by copies outside genes, 27 are lost with IRescue as main and 43 with scTE as main. Most of these are threshold effects, where the other method has log2FC 0.5–1. A few are real disagreements, e.g. MER110-int in ENP, which IRescue misses.
Rule
candidate up in IRescue or scTE-exclusive (padj < 0.05, log2FC > 1) → robust the other method agrees in direction (log2FC > 0.5) and nointron is not "intronic only" → otherwise discordant, with a reason: read_through, scte_only (IRescue counts only reads on the TE's own strand, scTE ignores strand, so possibly antisense), irescue_only (scTE drops reads in gene exons), or absent_in_irescue.
ATAC support: the subfamily itself, or one of its LTRs, is up in the same group by either ATAC method.
LTR pairing
The LTRs of each internal region are taken from the genome: RepeatMasker LTR-class elements within 50 bp of the -int fragments. A subfamily is listed if it makes up ≥ 15% of these flanks (≥ 20 flanks). This recovers the expected pairs: HERVH → LTR7, HERVS71 → LTR6B/6A, HERV15 → LTR15, HERVK → LTR5_Hs/5A/5B, HERVK11 → MER11A/B/C, HERV9 → LTR12/12F, HERVIP10B3 → LTR10B1/B2.
scripts/14_candidate_tiers.py
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
Tiered ERV candidate table: every RNA method on equal footing, plus read-through and ATAC evidence.

RNA calls come from 11_compare_scte_modes.py (IRescue = ir, scTE exclusive = ex, scTE nointron = no;
call = padj < 0.05 and log2FC > 1). For each subfamily x level (group or stage):
  candidate   up in IRescue OR scTE exclusive
  robust      the other method agrees in direction (log2FC > 0.5) and nointron is not intronic_only
  discordant  otherwise; `reasons` says why:
                read_through      nointron log2FC <= 0.5 (copies inside genes carry the signal)
                scte_only         IRescue flat; IRescue is sense-strand only, scTE unstranded ->
                                  candidate antisense transcription (or IRescue filtering)
                irescue_only      scTE exclusive flat; scTE drops reads on gene exons, IRescue keeps them
                absent_in_<m>     subfamily below the count filter of that method
ATAC: cut sites (05) and scTEATAC (05b) DESeq2 results, for the subfamily itself and for its LTRs.
  LTRs of an internal region are taken from the genome: RepeatMasker LTR-class elements within 50 bp
  of the -int fragments; an LTR subfamily is listed if it is >= 15% of those flanks (>= 20 flanks).
  atac_support = any of them up (padj < 0.05, log2FC > 1) in the same level by either ATAC method.
Small groups (< 200 cells in units) are flagged.

Outputs: $TE_OUT/qc/candidate_tiers_{group,stage}.csv, $TE_OUT/qc/erv_int_ltr_pairs.csv
"""
import os
import subprocess
from io import StringIO
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

TE_OUT = Path(os.environ["TE_OUT"]); D = TE_OUT / "deseq2"; qc = TE_OUT / "qc"
TE_ANNOT = Path(os.environ["TE_ANNOT_DIR"]); BEDTOOLS = Path(os.environ["TE_ENV"]) / "bin/bedtools"
pd.set_option("display.width", 250); pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 400); pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 60)


def int_ltr_pairs():
    """LTR subfamilies flanking each ERV internal subfamily in the genome."""
    rm = pd.read_csv(TE_ANNOT / "rmsk_hg38.bed.gz", sep="\t", header=None,
                     names=["chrom", "start", "end", "sub", "score", "strand", "family", "class"])
    rm = rm[rm["class"].str.rstrip("?") == "LTR"]
    is_int = rm["sub"].str.endswith("-int")
    tmp = qc / "tmp_pairs"; tmp.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    rm[is_int].iloc[:, :6].to_csv(tmp / "int.bed", sep="\t", header=False, index=False)
    rm[~is_int].iloc[:, :6].to_csv(tmp / "ltr.bed", sep="\t", header=False, index=False)
    out = subprocess.run([str(BEDTOOLS), "closest", "-a", str(tmp / "int.bed"), "-b", str(tmp / "ltr.bed"),
                          "-k", "2", "-d", "-t", "all"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    c = pd.read_csv(StringIO(out), sep="\t", header=None)
    c = c[(c[12] >= 0) & (c[12] <= 50)]
    n = c.groupby([3, 9]).size().rename("flanks").reset_index().rename(columns={3: "int", 9: "ltr"})
    n["share"] = n.flanks / n.groupby("int").flanks.transform("sum")
    pairs = n[(n.share >= 0.15) & (n.flanks >= 20)].sort_values(["int", "share"], ascending=[True, False])
    pairs.round(3).to_csv(qc / "erv_int_ltr_pairs.csv", index=False)
    for f in ["int.bed", "ltr.bed"]:
        (tmp / f).unlink()
    tmp.rmdir()
    return pairs.groupby("int").ltr.apply(list).to_dict()


pairs = int_ltr_pairs()
print("example pairings (genome-derived):", {k: pairs.get(k) for k in
      ["HERVH-int", "HERVS71-int", "HERV15-int", "HERVK-int", "HERVK11-int", "HERV9-int", "MER110-int",
       "MER92-int", "HERVIP10B3-int", "HERVIP10F-int", "PABL_A-int", "MLT1F2-int"]})


def atac_table(tag):
    a = {}
    for k, m in {"cut": "atac", "scte": "scte_atac"}.items():
        x = pd.read_csv(D / m / "results" / f"{tag}_vs_rest_all.csv").set_index(["subfamily", "level"])
        a[k] = x[["log2FoldChange", "padj"]]
    return a


def atac_evidence(sub, level, a):
    """Best ATAC evidence over the subfamily and its LTRs: (support, best_feature, lfc_cut, lfc_scte)."""
    feats = [sub] + pairs.get(sub, [])
    best = (False, "", np.nan, np.nan, -np.inf)
    for f in feats:
        lc = a["cut"].log2FoldChange.get((f, level), np.nan); pc = a["cut"].padj.get((f, level), np.nan)
        ls = a["scte"].log2FoldChange.get((f, level), np.nan); ps = a["scte"].padj.get((f, level), np.nan)
        up = (pc < 0.05 and lc > 1) or (ps < 0.05 and ls > 1)
        score = np.nanmax([lc, ls, -np.inf])
        if (up, score) > (best[0], best[4]):
            best = (up, f, lc, ls, score)
    return best[:4]


def tiers(tag):
    t = pd.read_csv(qc / f"scte_mode_comparison_{tag}.csv")
    t = t[(t["class"] == "LTR") & (t.up_ir | t.up_ex)].copy()
    agree = np.where(t.up_ir & t.up_ex, True,
                     np.where(t.up_ir, t.log2FoldChange_ex > 0.5, t.log2FoldChange_ir > 0.5))
    t["other_agrees"] = agree
    t["read_through"] = t.verdict.eq("intronic_only")
    t["tier"] = np.where(t.other_agrees & ~t.read_through, "robust", "discordant")

    def reasons(r):
        out = []
        if r.read_through:
            out.append("read_through")
        if not r.other_agrees:
            if r.up_ex and not r.up_ir:
                out.append("absent_in_irescue" if np.isnan(r.log2FoldChange_ir) else "scte_only")
            else:
                out.append("absent_in_scte" if np.isnan(r.log2FoldChange_ex) else "irescue_only")
        return ",".join(out)
    t["reasons"] = t.apply(reasons, axis=1)

    a = atac_table(tag)
    ev = [atac_evidence(s, l, a) for s, l in zip(t.subfamily, t.level)]
    t["atac_support"] = [e[0] for e in ev]
    t["atac_feature"] = [e[1] for e in ev]
    t["atac_lfc_cut"] = [e[2] for e in ev]
    t["atac_lfc_scte"] = [e[3] for e in ev]
    t["paired_ltrs"] = [";".join(pairs.get(s, [])) for s in t.subfamily]
    if tag == "group":
        cells = pd.read_csv(D / "rna/coldata.csv").groupby("group").n_cells.sum()
        t["group_cells"] = t.level.map(cells).values
        t["small_group"] = t.group_cells < 200
    cols = ["subfamily", "family", "level", "tier", "reasons", "baseMean_ir", "log2FoldChange_ir", "padj_ir",
            "log2FoldChange_ex", "padj_ex", "log2FoldChange_no", "padj_no", "verdict", "frac_ratio",
            "atac_support", "atac_feature", "atac_lfc_cut", "atac_lfc_scte", "paired_ltrs"] + \
           (["group_cells", "small_group"] if tag == "group" else [])
    t = t[cols].sort_values(["level", "tier", "log2FoldChange_ir"], ascending=[True, False, False])
    t.round(3).to_csv(qc / f"candidate_tiers_{tag}.csv", index=False)

    print(f"\n===== {tag}: {len(t)} ERV/LTR candidates; robust {(t.tier == 'robust').sum()} "
          f"({t[t.tier == 'robust'].atac_support.sum()} with ATAC support); discordant {(t.tier == 'discordant').sum()}")
    print("discordant reasons:", t[t.tier == "discordant"].reasons.value_counts().to_dict())
    show = ["subfamily", "level", "tier", "reasons", "log2FoldChange_ir", "log2FoldChange_ex", "log2FoldChange_no",
            "atac_support", "atac_feature", "atac_lfc_cut", "atac_lfc_scte"]
    big = t[(t.baseMean_ir.fillna(0) > 20) | (t.log2FoldChange_ex > 1.5)]
    print(big[show].round(2).to_string(index=False), flush=True)
    return t


tiers("group")
tiers("stage")
print("done", qc)

4.13 Locus level

What
IRescue -l, sense strand only, on every RepeatMasker LTR-class copy (725,763). Each copy has a unique ID <subfamily>|chrom_start_end_strand. Then:
  1. pseudobulk into the 119 units;
  2. annotate each copy as intergenic, intronic or exonic, with its host gene and whether it lies sense or antisense to it (Cell Ranger GTF);
  3. for each candidate, rank copies by their share of the increase and report n50, the number of copies giving 50% of it.
Why
A subfamily call can come from one active copy. Naming the copies shows whether an induction is a single-locus event, many copies, or a host gene. This also keeps solo LTRs (LTR12_, MLT1F2), which the Telescope proviral annotation lacks.
Checks
On sample 10, per-copy totals summed by subfamily match the subfamily run (r = 0.998), about 10% higher because LINE/SINE copies no longer compete for reads. That run took 3 min and 29 GB.
scripts/15_irescue_locus.sb
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=12
#SBATCH --mem=110G
#SBATCH --time=24:00:00
#SBATCH --partition=acpu
#SBATCH --qos=cpu-normal
#SBATCH --array=1-15%5
#SBATCH --job-name=irescue_locus
#SBATCH --output=logs/irescue_locus.%A_%a.out
# Locus-level RNA counts (IRescue -l) for every RepeatMasker LTR-class copy (ERVs and solo LTRs, 725,763),
# to name the copies behind the subfamily calls and check their host-gene context.
#   - feature ID (BED column 4) = "<subfamily>|<chrom>_<start>_<end>_<strand>", unique per copy;
#     IRescue keeps it as the feature name
#   - multi-mapping reads are shared between copies by IRescue's EM (per cell, per UMI); counts at
#     individual young copies (HERVK HML-2, HERVH) are estimates, not unique evidence
#   - forward-stranded (sense to the copy only), as the subfamily run (03); subfamily mode used ~40 GB,
#     locus mode is given 110 GB
# Output: $TE_OUT/irescue_locus/<sample>/counts/. Usage: sbatch [--array=10] scripts/15_irescue_locus.sb
set -euo pipefail
source config.sh
export PATH="$TE_ENV/bin:$PATH"
bed="$TE_ANNOT_DIR/irescue/ltr_loci.bed"
if [ ! -s "$bed" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$bed")"
  zcat "$TE_ANNOT_DIR/rmsk_hg38.bed.gz" \
    | awk -v OFS='\t' '$8 ~ /^LTR/ { print $1, $2, $3, $4 "|" $1 "_" $2 "_" $3 "_" $6, 0, $6 }' > "$bed.tmp"
  mv "$bed.tmp" "$bed"
fi
row=$(awk -F'\t' -v t="${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}" 'NR>1 && $1==t' configs/samples.tsv)
sample=$(cut -f2 <<<"$row"); gex_bam=$(cut -f4 <<<"$row")
wl="$TE_OUT/whitelists/${sample}.txt"
echo "task ${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}: ${sample} ($(wc -l < "$wl") cells), $(wc -l < "$bed") LTR loci"
out="$TE_OUT/irescue_locus/${sample}"; mkdir -p "$out"
irescue -b "$gex_bam" -r "$bed" -w "$wl" -c CB -u UB -l \
  --strandedness forward --integers -p "$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK" -o "$out" -v
ls -la "$out/counts"
scripts/16_locus_candidates.py
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
Name the copies behind each ERV candidate (14_candidate_tiers.py) from the IRescue locus counts (15).

1. Pseudobulk the per-cell locus counts into the 119 RNA units (sample x group, as 07):
   $TE_OUT/irescue_locus/locus_units.npz (+ _loci.txt, _units.csv). Expression = UMIs per million gene UMIs.
2. Host-gene context of every LTR-class copy, from the Cell Ranger ARC GTF (same genes as the RNA):
   intergenic / intronic / exonic, the gene name, and whether the copy is sense or antisense to it.
3. For each candidate subfamily x group: delta_i = CPM in the group - mean CPM over the other groups,
   per copy i. Copies are ranked by delta; reported are the copies that make up 80% of the summed
   positive delta, with their context and how many of the group's units show them (> 2x rest mean).
   n50 = number of copies giving 50% of the increase (1-2 = driven by single loci).

Outputs: $TE_OUT/qc/locus_candidates_{group}.csv (one row per candidate x copy),
         $TE_OUT/qc/locus_candidate_summary.csv (one row per candidate),
         $TE_OUT/qc/ltr_loci_context.csv.gz
"""
import os
import subprocess
from io import StringIO
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import scipy.io
import scipy.sparse as sp

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TE_OUT = Path(os.environ["TE_OUT"]); ANNOT = Path(os.environ["ANNOTATION_CSV"]); SCP_OUT = Path(os.environ["SCP_OUT"])
TE_ANNOT = Path(os.environ["TE_ANNOT_DIR"]); BEDTOOLS = str(Path(os.environ["TE_ENV"]) / "bin/bedtools")
qc = TE_OUT / "qc"; LOC = TE_OUT / "irescue_locus"
pd.set_option("display.width", 250); pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 500)

# ---------- 1. pseudobulk locus counts into the RNA units
units_ref = pd.read_csv(TE_OUT / "deseq2/rna/coldata.csv", index_col=0)
units = units_ref.index
ann = pd.read_csv(ANNOT, index_col=0, dtype=str)
ann = ann[ann.include_downstream.str.lower() == "true"]
npz = LOC / "locus_units.npz"
if npz.exists():
    M = sp.load_npz(npz).tocsr(); loci = pd.Index(Path(LOC / "locus_units_loci.txt").read_text().split("\n"))
else:
    samples = pd.read_csv(REPO / "configs/samples.tsv", sep="\t")["sample"].tolist()
    loci = pd.Index(pd.read_csv(TE_ANNOT / "irescue/ltr_loci.bed", sep="\t", header=None, usecols=[3])[3])
    M = sp.csr_matrix((len(units), len(loci)), dtype=np.float64)
    for s in samples:
        d = LOC / s / "counts"
        m = scipy.io.mmread(d / "matrix.mtx.gz").tocsr().T          # cells x features
        f = pd.read_csv(d / "features.tsv.gz", sep="\t", header=None)[0].values
        b = s + "#" + pd.read_csv(d / "barcodes.tsv.gz", header=None)[0].astype(str)
        grp = ann["ATAC_WNN_annotation"].reindex(b).astype(str).values
        codes = units.get_indexer(s + "__" + pd.Series(grp))
        keep = codes >= 0
        ind = sp.csr_matrix((np.ones(keep.sum()), (codes[keep], np.where(keep)[0])), shape=(len(units), m.shape[0]))
        part = (ind @ m).tocoo()
        M = M + sp.csr_matrix((part.data, (part.row, loci.get_indexer(f)[part.col])), shape=M.shape)
        print(f"{s}: {m.shape[0]} cells, {m.shape[1]} expressed loci, {m.sum():,.0f} UMIs", flush=True)
    sp.save_npz(npz, M.tocsr()); Path(LOC / "locus_units_loci.txt").write_text("\n".join(loci))
    units_ref.to_csv(LOC / "locus_units_units.csv")
cpm = sp.diags(1e6 / units_ref.lib_size.values) @ M                 # units x loci, per million gene UMIs
groups = units_ref.group.values
G = pd.Index(sorted(set(groups)))
gi = sp.csr_matrix((np.ones(len(units)) / pd.Series(groups).map(pd.Series(groups).value_counts()).values,
                    (G.get_indexer(groups), np.arange(len(units)))), shape=(len(G), len(units)))
gcpm = (gi @ cpm).tocsr()                                            # group mean of unit CPMs, groups x loci

# ---------- 2. host-gene context of each copy
ctx_file = qc / "ltr_loci_context.csv.gz"
if ctx_file.exists():
    ctx = pd.read_csv(ctx_file, index_col=0)
else:
    gtf = TE_ANNOT / "scte/genes.gtf"
    rows = []
    with open(gtf) as fh:
        for line in fh:
            if line.startswith("#"):
                continue
            t = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
            if t[2] not in ("gene", "exon"):
                continue
            name = t[8].split('gene_name "')[1].split('"')[0]
            rows.append((t[0], int(t[3]) - 1, int(t[4]), name, t[2], t[6]))
    g = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["chrom", "start", "end", "gene", "kind", "strand"])
    tmp = qc / "tmp_ctx"; tmp.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    for k in ("gene", "exon"):
        g[g.kind == k].sort_values(["chrom", "start"])[["chrom", "start", "end", "gene", "kind", "strand"]] \
            .to_csv(tmp / f"{k}.bed", sep="\t", header=False, index=False)
    lb = TE_ANNOT / "irescue/ltr_loci.bed"

    def hits(k):
        out = subprocess.run([BEDTOOLS, "intersect", "-a", str(lb), "-b", str(tmp / f"{k}.bed"), "-wa", "-wb"],
                             capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
        h = pd.read_csv(StringIO(out), sep="\t", header=None, usecols=[3, 5, 9, 11], names=["locus", "te_strand", "gene", "g_strand"])
        h["orient"] = np.where(h.te_strand == h.g_strand, "sense", "antisense")
        return h.groupby("locus").agg(gene=("gene", lambda x: ",".join(sorted(set(x)))),
                                      orient=("orient", lambda x: ",".join(sorted(set(x)))))
    ex, ge = hits("exon"), hits("gene")
    for f in ("gene.bed", "exon.bed"):
        (tmp / f).unlink()
    tmp.rmdir()
    ctx = pd.DataFrame(index=loci)
    ctx["context"] = np.where(ctx.index.isin(ex.index), "exonic", np.where(ctx.index.isin(ge.index), "intronic", "intergenic"))
    ctx["host_gene"] = ge.gene.reindex(ctx.index)
    ctx["orientation"] = ge.orient.reindex(ctx.index)
    ctx.to_csv(ctx_file)
print("copy context:", ctx.context.value_counts().to_dict(), flush=True)

# ---------- 3. copies behind each candidate
cand = pd.read_csv(qc / "candidate_tiers_group.csv")
sub_of = pd.Series([l.split("|")[0] for l in loci], index=loci)
by_sub = pd.Series(np.arange(len(loci))).groupby(sub_of.values).apply(list)
rows, summ = [], []
for r in cand.itertuples():
    if r.subfamily not in by_sub.index:
        continue
    idx = np.array(by_sub[r.subfamily]); g = G.get_loc(r.level)
    gc = gcpm[:, idx].toarray()
    in_g = gc[g]; rest = np.delete(gc, g, axis=0).mean(0)
    delta = in_g - rest
    pos = np.where(delta > 0)[0]
    tot = delta[pos].sum()
    if tot <= 0:
        summ.append((r.subfamily, r.level, r.tier, r.reasons, 0, np.nan, np.nan, "", ""))
        continue
    order = pos[np.argsort(-delta[pos])]
    cum = np.cumsum(delta[order]) / tot
    n50 = int(np.searchsorted(cum, 0.5) + 1); n80 = int(np.searchsorted(cum, 0.8) + 1)
    u = np.where(groups == r.level)[0]
    ucpm = cpm[u][:, idx].toarray()
    for k, j in enumerate(order[:min(n80, 25)]):
        lid = loci[idx[j]]
        rows.append({"subfamily": r.subfamily, "level": r.level, "tier": r.tier, "reasons": r.reasons, "rank": k + 1,
                     "locus": lid.split("|")[1], "cpm_group": in_g[j], "cpm_rest": rest[j],
                     "log2fc": np.log2((in_g[j] + 0.5) / (rest[j] + 0.5)), "share_of_increase": delta[j] / tot,
                     "units_up": f"{int((ucpm[:, j] > 2 * rest[j]).sum())}/{len(u)}",
                     "context": ctx.context.get(lid), "host_gene": ctx.host_gene.get(lid), "orientation": ctx.orientation.get(lid)})
    top = [x for x in rows if x["subfamily"] == r.subfamily and x["level"] == r.level][:n50]
    ctx_share = pd.Series({c: sum(x["share_of_increase"] for x in rows if x["subfamily"] == r.subfamily
                                  and x["level"] == r.level and x["context"] == c) for c in ["intergenic", "intronic", "exonic"]})
    summ.append((r.subfamily, r.level, r.tier, r.reasons, len(pos), n50, n80,
                 "; ".join(f"{x['locus']} ({x['context']}{', ' + str(x['host_gene']) if x['host_gene'] == x['host_gene'] and x['host_gene'] else ''})" for x in top[:3]),
                 ", ".join(f"{c} {v:.0%}" for c, v in ctx_share.items() if v > 0)))
loc = pd.DataFrame(rows)
loc.round(4).to_csv(qc / "locus_candidates_group.csv", index=False)
s = pd.DataFrame(summ, columns=["subfamily", "level", "tier", "reasons", "copies_up", "n50", "n80", "top_copies", "context_of_top80"])
s.to_csv(qc / "locus_candidate_summary.csv", index=False)
print(s[s.tier == "robust"].to_string(index=False))
print("\ndiscordant:\n", s[s.tier != "robust"].to_string(index=False))
print("done", qc)

4.14 ZNF808 / MER11 check

Why
De Franco et al. 2023: loss of the primate-specific KZFP ZNF808 causes pancreatic agenesis. ZNF808 represses MER11A/B/C, and in knockout differentiations MER11 copies gain activity (some at the pancreatic progenitor stage) while progenitors switch on liver genes. Our protocol makes off-target liver-like cells. Do they look like partial ZNF808 failure?
How
ZNF808, TRIM28, SETDB1 and marker genes are read from the shared counts layer, column-wise without loading the 10 GB matrix, and summed into the 119 units. MER11A/B/C and HERVK11-int signal comes from all five TE count tables on the same units. Groups are compared, especially liver vs PP1/PP2/FG.
scripts/17_znf808_mer11.py
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
ZNF808 / MER11 check in the wild-type time course.

De Franco et al. 2023 (Nat Genet, ZNF808 pancreatic agenesis): ZNF808 binds MER11A/B/C; in ZNF808-KO
differentiations MER11 copies gain H3K27ac (some at the pancreatic progenitor stage) and progenitors
switch on liver genes (AFP, ALB, APOA1). Our differentiations make off-target liver-like cells, so ask:
across cell groups, is ZNF808 (and the KZFP co-repressors TRIM28 / SETDB1) lower where MER11 is more
transcribed or more open, in particular liver vs PP1/PP2/FG?

Gene counts: shared RNA object, layers/counts (read column-wise from the CSR without loading it all),
summed into the 119 RNA units, per million gene UMIs (lib_size of 07). MER11 signal: every TE count
table on the same units -- IRescue, scTE exclusive / nointron (RNA), cut sites / scTEATAC (ATAC).
Outputs: $TE_OUT/qc/znf808_mer11_by_group.csv, znf808_mer11.png
"""
import os
from pathlib import Path

import h5py
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

TE_OUT = Path(os.environ["TE_OUT"]); SCP_OUT = Path(os.environ["SCP_OUT"]); ANNOT = Path(os.environ["ANNOTATION_CSV"])
D = TE_OUT / "deseq2"; qc = TE_OUT / "qc"
GENES = ["ZNF808", "TRIM28", "SETDB1", "AFP", "ALB", "APOA1", "PDX1", "NKX6-1", "INS"]
SUBS = ["MER11A", "MER11B", "MER11C", "HERVK11-int"]
ORDER = ["hPSC", "DE", "GT", "OTX2_endo", "FG", "liver", "PP1", "PP2", "ENP1", "ENP2", "ENP3", "early_SC_beta",
         "early_EC_beta", "early_SC_alpha", "early_SC_delta", "early_SC_EC", "late_SC_beta", "late_EC_beta",
         "late_SC_alpha", "late_SC_delta", "late_SC_EC", "ductal", "exocrine", "stroma"]
pd.set_option("display.width", 250)

units = pd.read_csv(D / "rna/coldata.csv", index_col=0)
ann = pd.read_csv(ANNOT, index_col=0, dtype=str)

# ---- gene counts for a few genes, from the CSR counts layer, chunked over rows
with h5py.File(SCP_OUT / "integration/h5ad/merged_rna_scvi_integrated.h5ad", "r") as f:
    cells = f["obs"]["_index"][:].astype(str)
    var = f["var"]["_index"][:].astype(str)
    cols = {g: int(np.where(var == g)[0][0]) for g in GENES}
    L = f["layers"]["counts"]; indptr = L["indptr"][:]
    gx = np.zeros((len(cells), len(GENES)), dtype=np.float32)
    colidx = np.array(list(cols.values()))
    step = 5000
    for a in range(0, len(cells), step):
        b = min(a + step, len(cells))
        idx = L["indices"][indptr[a]:indptr[b]]; dat = L["data"][indptr[a]:indptr[b]]
        row = np.repeat(np.arange(a, b), np.diff(indptr[a:b + 1]))
        for k, c in enumerate(colidx):
            m = idx == c
            np.add.at(gx[:, k], row[m], dat[m])
gx = pd.DataFrame(gx, index=cells, columns=GENES)
grp = ann["ATAC_WNN_annotation"].reindex(gx.index).astype(str)
unit = pd.Series([c.split("#")[0] for c in gx.index], index=gx.index) + "__" + grp
gu = gx.groupby(unit.values).sum().reindex(units.index)
gcpm = gu.div(units.lib_size, axis=0) * 1e6

# ---- MER11 counts on the same units from every method
te = {}
for name, m, lib in [("IRescue", "rna", "rna"), ("scTE_excl", "scte_exclusive", "rna"), ("scTE_nointron", "scte_nointron", "rna"),
                     ("ATAC_cut", "atac", "atac"), ("ATAC_scTE", "scte_atac", "atac")]:
    c = pd.read_csv(D / m / "counts.csv", index_col=0).reindex(SUBS).T
    cd = pd.read_csv(D / m / "coldata.csv", index_col=0)
    te[name] = c.div(cd.lib_size.reindex(c.index), axis=0) * 1e6
by_group = {}
G = units.group
for g, d in gcpm.groupby(G):
    row = {f"{x}_cpm": d[x].mean() for x in GENES}
    for name, t in te.items():
        tt = t.reindex(d.index)
        for s in SUBS:
            row[f"{s}|{name}"] = tt[s].mean()
    row["units"] = len(d); row["cells"] = units.loc[d.index, "n_cells"].sum()
    by_group[g] = row
bg = pd.DataFrame(by_group).T.reindex([o for o in ORDER if o in by_group])
bg.round(3).to_csv(qc / "znf808_mer11_by_group.csv")

print("genes per group (CPM, mean of units):\n", bg[[f"{x}_cpm" for x in GENES] + ["cells"]].round(1).to_string())
mer = bg[[c for c in bg.columns if c.startswith("MER11") or c.startswith("HERVK11")]]
print("\nMER11 / HERVK11 per group (per million gene UMIs or cut sites):\n", mer.round(1).to_string())
big = bg[bg.cells >= 200]
print("\nSpearman across groups (>= 200 cells): ZNF808 vs MER11 signal")
for c in mer.columns:
    print(f"  {c:28s} rho = {big['ZNF808_cpm'].corr(big[c], method='spearman'):+.2f}")
print("\nliver vs PP1/PP2/FG (ratio of group means):")
for c in ["ZNF808_cpm", "TRIM28_cpm"] + list(mer.columns):
    print(f"  {c:28s} liver/PP1 {bg.loc['liver', c] / bg.loc['PP1', c]:.2f}  liver/PP2 {bg.loc['liver', c] / bg.loc['PP2', c]:.2f}  "
          f"liver/FG {bg.loc['liver', c] / bg.loc['FG', c]:.2f}")

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(17, 4.6), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.3, 1, 1]})
x = np.arange(len(bg))
axes[0].bar(x, bg.ZNF808_cpm, color=["#b2182b" if g == "liver" else "#2166ac" if g in ("PP1", "PP2") else "#999999" for g in bg.index])
axes[0].set_xticks(x, bg.index, rotation=70, ha="right", fontsize=8); axes[0].set_ylabel("ZNF808, UMIs per million gene UMIs")
axes[0].set_title("ZNF808 by group (liver red, PP blue)")
for ax, mod in zip(axes[1:], ["scTE_nointron", "ATAC_cut"]):
    for s, col in zip(SUBS, ["#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3", "#444444"]):
        v = big[f"{s}|{mod}"]
        ax.scatter(big.ZNF808_cpm, v, s=18, c=col, label=s)
        for g in ("liver", "PP1", "PP2", "FG", "hPSC"):
            if g in big.index:
                ax.annotate(g, (big.loc[g, "ZNF808_cpm"], big.loc[g, f"{s}|{mod}"]), fontsize=6, alpha=.7)
    ax.set_xlabel("ZNF808 (CPM)"); ax.set_ylabel(f"MER11 signal, {mod}"); ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.set_title(f"ZNF808 vs MER11 ({mod})")
axes[1].legend(fontsize=7, frameon=False)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(qc / "znf808_mer11.png", dpi=110)
print("done", qc)
scripts/19_mer11_copies.py (per-copy MER11 in liver vs PP/FG)
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
ZNF808 / MER11 at copy level (follows 17_znf808_mer11.py, which found no subfamily-level signal).

Do individual MER11A/B/C copies switch on in the liver-like off-target cells compared with the
pancreatic progenitors (PP1, PP2) and foregut (FG) they branch from? Uses the IRescue locus pseudobulk
($TE_OUT/irescue_locus/locus_units.npz from 16): UMIs per million gene UMIs, unit means per group.
A copy is "liver-on" if liver >= 2 CPM, log2((liver+0.5)/(max(PP1,PP2,FG)+0.5)) >= 2, and it is up
(> 2x the PP/FG maximum) in at least half of the liver units. Reported with host / nearest genes.
Comparison: the same rule for every other LTR-class subfamily, to see whether MER11 stands out.

Outputs: $TE_OUT/qc/mer11_liver_copies.csv, mer11_vs_other_subfamilies.csv
"""
import os
import subprocess
from io import StringIO
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import scipy.sparse as sp

TE_OUT = Path(os.environ["TE_OUT"]); TE_ANNOT = Path(os.environ["TE_ANNOT_DIR"])
BEDTOOLS = str(Path(os.environ["TE_ENV"]) / "bin/bedtools")
qc = TE_OUT / "qc"; LOC = TE_OUT / "irescue_locus"
pd.set_option("display.width", 250)

M = sp.load_npz(LOC / "locus_units.npz").tocsr()
loci = pd.Index((LOC / "locus_units_loci.txt").read_text().split("\n"))
units = pd.read_csv(LOC / "locus_units_units.csv", index_col=0)
cpm = (sp.diags(1e6 / units.lib_size.values) @ M).tocsc()
grp = units.group.values


def gmean(g):
    return np.asarray(cpm[grp == g].mean(0)).ravel()


liver, pp1, pp2, fg = gmean("liver"), gmean("PP1"), gmean("PP2"), gmean("FG")
ref = np.maximum.reduce([pp1, pp2, fg])
lfc = np.log2((liver + 0.5) / (ref + 0.5))
lu = cpm[grp == "liver"].toarray()
units_up = (lu > 2 * ref[None, :]).sum(0)
n_liver = (grp == "liver").sum()
on = (liver >= 2) & (lfc >= 2) & (units_up >= n_liver / 2)
sub = pd.Series([l.split("|")[0] for l in loci], index=loci)

# per subfamily: fraction of expressed copies that are liver-on
expressed = (np.maximum(liver, ref) >= 2)
tab = pd.DataFrame({"sub": sub.values, "on": on, "expr": expressed}).groupby("sub").agg(
    copies=("on", "size"), expressed=("expr", "sum"), liver_on=("on", "sum"))
tab = tab[tab.expressed >= 20]
tab["frac_on"] = tab.liver_on / tab.expressed
tab["rank"] = tab.frac_on.rank(ascending=False)
tab.sort_values("frac_on", ascending=False).round(3).to_csv(qc / "mer11_vs_other_subfamilies.csv")
print(f"LTR subfamilies with >= 20 expressed copies: {len(tab)}; median fraction liver-on {tab.frac_on.median():.3f}")
print(tab.loc[[s for s in ["MER11A", "MER11B", "MER11C", "HERVK11-int"] if s in tab.index]].round(3).to_string())
print("top 15 subfamilies by fraction of liver-on copies:\n", tab.sort_values("frac_on", ascending=False).head(15).round(3).to_string())

mer = np.where(sub.str.match(r"^(MER11[ABC]|HERVK11-int)$").values & on)[0]
out = pd.DataFrame({"locus": loci[mer], "liver": liver[mer], "PP1": pp1[mer], "PP2": pp2[mer], "FG": fg[mer],
                    "log2fc_vs_max": lfc[mer], "liver_units_up": [f"{u}/{n_liver}" for u in units_up[mer]]})
ctx = pd.read_csv(qc / "ltr_loci_context.csv.gz", index_col=0)
out = out.join(ctx, on="locus")
if len(out):
    p = out.locus.str.split("|").str[1].str.rsplit("_", n=3, expand=True)
    bed = pd.DataFrame({"c": p[0], "s": p[1].astype(int), "e": p[2].astype(int), "id": out.locus}).sort_values(["c", "s"])
    bed.to_csv(qc / "tmp_mer11.bed", sep="\t", header=False, index=False)
    genes = []
    for line in open(TE_ANNOT / "scte/genes.gtf"):
        t = line.split("\t", 9)
        if len(t) > 8 and t[2] == "gene" and 'gene_type "protein_coding"' in t[8]:
            genes.append((t[0], int(t[3]) - 1, int(t[4]), t[8].split('gene_name "')[1].split('"')[0]))
    pd.DataFrame(genes).sort_values([0, 1]).to_csv(qc / "tmp_pc.bed", sep="\t", header=False, index=False)
    cl = pd.read_csv(StringIO(subprocess.run([BEDTOOLS, "closest", "-a", str(qc / "tmp_mer11.bed"), "-b", str(qc / "tmp_pc.bed"),
                                              "-k", "2", "-d", "-t", "all"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout),
                     sep="\t", header=None)
    out["nearest_pc"] = out.locus.map(cl.groupby(3).apply(lambda d: "; ".join(f"{g} {int(x) // 1000}kb" for g, x in zip(d[7], d[8]))))
    (qc / "tmp_mer11.bed").unlink(); (qc / "tmp_pc.bed").unlink()
out.sort_values("log2fc_vs_max", ascending=False).round(2).to_csv(qc / "mer11_liver_copies.csv", index=False)
print(f"\nMER11A/B/C / HERVK11-int copies on in liver (vs max of PP1, PP2, FG): {len(out)}")
print(out.sort_values("liver", ascending=False).round(2).to_string(index=False))
print("done", qc)

4.15 Copy follow-up

18
For the top copies of each candidate:
  • segmental duplication identity (UCSC genomicSuperDups, fetched on acompile). At ≥ 0.98, reads can be shared with a paralog, so the exact copy is uncertain even if the region's signal is real.
  • the 3 nearest protein-coding genes;
  • whether the host gene or nearby genes go up in the same group, from the shared gene counts.
Host gene up → read-through or an ERV exon. Nearby gene up → possible enhancer. Nothing up → an autonomous ERV transcript.
20
Per-copy ATAC: Tn5 cut sites from the fragment files (tabix) in each copy ± 3 kb, which includes its LTRs. Summed into units and scaled by total cut sites.
21
The chr5 HERV9 provirus in detail: RNA per part (IRescue per copy) and ATAC in 5 windows (5′ LTR, internal halves, 3′ LTR, downstream).
scripts/18_locus_followup.py
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
Follow-up on the copies behind each ERV candidate (16_locus_candidates.py): neighbourhood, duplication
and whether the host / nearby genes are induced in the same group.

For the top copies of every candidate (rank <= 5 and >= 5% of the increase):
  - segmental duplication: highest fractional identity of an overlapping UCSC genomicSuperDups pair
    ($TE_ANNOT_DIR/segdups_hg38.bed); >= 0.98 means reads can be shared with a paralog, so the copy
    assignment (not the regional signal) is uncertain
  - the 3 nearest protein-coding genes (Cell Ranger GTF; distance 0 = overlapping)
  - for the host gene(s) and the nearest genes: expression in the candidate's group vs the mean of the
    other groups (UMIs per million gene UMIs, unit means, from the shared counts layer), log2FC
    -> host gene up with the copy = read-through / ERV exon; nearby gene up = possible LTR enhancer or
       promoter; nothing up = autonomous ERV transcript
Also lists clusters: copies of different candidates within 2 Mb of each other.

Outputs: $TE_OUT/qc/locus_followup.csv, $TE_OUT/qc/locus_clusters.csv
"""
import os
import subprocess
from io import StringIO
from pathlib import Path

import h5py
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

TE_OUT = Path(os.environ["TE_OUT"]); SCP_OUT = Path(os.environ["SCP_OUT"]); ANNOT = Path(os.environ["ANNOTATION_CSV"])
TE_ANNOT = Path(os.environ["TE_ANNOT_DIR"]); BEDTOOLS = str(Path(os.environ["TE_ENV"]) / "bin/bedtools")
qc = TE_OUT / "qc"; tmp = qc / "tmp_followup"; tmp.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
pd.set_option("display.width", 250); pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 400); pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 70)

loc = pd.read_csv(qc / "locus_candidates_group.csv")
loc = loc[(loc["rank"] <= 5) & (loc.share_of_increase >= 0.05)].copy()
parts = loc.locus.str.rsplit("_", n=3, expand=True)
loc["chrom"], loc["start"], loc["end"], loc["strand"] = parts[0], parts[1].astype(int), parts[2].astype(int), parts[3]
copies = loc[["chrom", "start", "end", "locus"]].drop_duplicates().sort_values(["chrom", "start"])
copies.to_csv(tmp / "copies.bed", sep="\t", header=False, index=False)


def run(*args):
    return subprocess.run([BEDTOOLS, *args], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout


# ---- segmental duplications
sd = pd.read_csv(StringIO(run("intersect", "-a", str(tmp / "copies.bed"), "-b", str(TE_ANNOT / "segdups_hg38.bed"), "-wa", "-wb")),
                 sep="\t", header=None)
segdup = sd.groupby(3)[8].max() if len(sd) else pd.Series(dtype=float)
loc["segdup_identity"] = loc.locus.map(segdup)

# ---- protein-coding genes, nearest 3
rows = []
with open(TE_ANNOT / "scte/genes.gtf") as fh:
    for line in fh:
        if line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        t = line.split("\t", 9)
        if t[2] != "gene":
            continue
        a = t[8]
        name = a.split('gene_name "')[1].split('"')[0]
        gtype = a.split('gene_type "')[1].split('"')[0] if 'gene_type "' in a else ""
        rows.append((t[0], int(t[3]) - 1, int(t[4]), name, gtype, t[6]))
genes = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["chrom", "start", "end", "gene", "type", "strand"])
pc = genes[genes.type == "protein_coding"].sort_values(["chrom", "start"])
pc[["chrom", "start", "end", "gene", "type", "strand"]].to_csv(tmp / "pc.bed", sep="\t", header=False, index=False)
cl = pd.read_csv(StringIO(run("closest", "-a", str(tmp / "copies.bed"), "-b", str(tmp / "pc.bed"), "-k", "3", "-d", "-t", "all")),
                 sep="\t", header=None)
near = cl.groupby(3).apply(lambda d: list(zip(d[7], d[10])))
loc["nearest_pc"] = loc.locus.map(lambda l: "; ".join(f"{g} {int(dist) // 1000}kb" for g, dist in near.get(l, [])))

# ---- gene expression per group for host + nearest genes
want = set()
for h in loc.host_gene.dropna():
    want.update(h.split(","))
for l in near.index:
    want.update(g for g, _ in near[l])
units = pd.read_csv(TE_OUT / "deseq2/rna/coldata.csv", index_col=0)
ann = pd.read_csv(ANNOT, index_col=0, dtype=str)
with h5py.File(SCP_OUT / "integration/h5ad/merged_rna_scvi_integrated.h5ad", "r") as f:
    cells = f["obs"]["_index"][:].astype(str)
    var = pd.Index(f["var"]["_index"][:].astype(str))
    gl = [g for g in sorted(want) if g in var]
    col = var.get_indexer(gl)
    pos = {c: k for k, c in enumerate(col)}
    L = f["layers"]["counts"]; indptr = L["indptr"][:]
    gx = np.zeros((len(cells), len(gl)), dtype=np.float32)
    for a in range(0, len(cells), 5000):
        b = min(a + 5000, len(cells))
        idx = L["indices"][indptr[a]:indptr[b]]; dat = L["data"][indptr[a]:indptr[b]]
        row = np.repeat(np.arange(a, b), np.diff(indptr[a:b + 1]))
        m = np.isin(idx, col)
        np.add.at(gx, (row[m], np.array([pos[c] for c in idx[m]], dtype=int)), dat[m])
gx = pd.DataFrame(gx, index=cells, columns=gl)
unit = pd.Series([c.split("#")[0] for c in cells], index=cells) + "__" + ann["ATAC_WNN_annotation"].reindex(cells).astype(str).values
gu = gx.groupby(unit.values).sum().reindex(units.index)
cpm = gu.div(units.lib_size, axis=0) * 1e6
gmean = cpm.groupby(units.group).mean()


def gene_fc(genes_, level):
    out = []
    for g in genes_:
        if g not in gmean.columns:
            continue
        a = gmean.loc[level, g]; r = gmean.drop(level)[g].mean()
        out.append(f"{g} {a:.1f}/{r:.1f} ({np.log2((a + 0.5) / (r + 0.5)):+.1f})")
    return "; ".join(out)


loc["host_expr"] = [gene_fc(h.split(","), l) if isinstance(h, str) else "" for h, l in zip(loc.host_gene, loc.level)]
loc["nearest_expr"] = [gene_fc([g for g, _ in near.get(c, [])], l) for c, l in zip(loc.locus, loc.level)]
cols = ["subfamily", "level", "tier", "reasons", "rank", "locus", "cpm_group", "cpm_rest", "log2fc", "share_of_increase",
        "units_up", "context", "host_gene", "orientation", "segdup_identity", "host_expr", "nearest_pc", "nearest_expr"]
loc[cols].round(3).to_csv(qc / "locus_followup.csv", index=False)

# ---- clusters of copies across candidates (same chromosome, within 2 Mb)
c = loc.sort_values(["chrom", "start"])
clusters, cur = [], []
for r in c.itertuples():
    if cur and (r.chrom != cur[-1].chrom or r.start - cur[-1].end > 2_000_000):
        clusters.append(cur); cur = []
    cur.append(r)
clusters.append(cur)
cl_rows = []
for k in clusters:
    cands = sorted({f"{x.subfamily}@{x.level}" for x in k})
    if len(cands) >= 3:
        cl_rows.append({"region": f"{k[0].chrom}:{min(x.start for x in k):,}-{max(x.end for x in k):,}",
                        "n_copies": len({x.locus for x in k}), "candidates": ", ".join(cands),
                        "max_segdup": np.nanmax([x.segdup_identity for x in k] + [np.nan])})
pd.DataFrame(cl_rows).to_csv(qc / "locus_clusters.csv", index=False)

show = ["subfamily", "level", "tier", "rank", "locus", "share_of_increase", "units_up", "context", "segdup_identity", "host_expr", "nearest_expr"]
print(loc[show].round(2).to_string(index=False))
print("\nclusters (>= 3 candidate x group combinations within 2 Mb):\n", pd.DataFrame(cl_rows).to_string(index=False))
for f in tmp.iterdir():
    f.unlink()
tmp.rmdir()
print("done", qc)
scripts/20_locus_atac.py
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
Chromatin at the copies behind each ERV candidate: Tn5 cut sites in each copy's region, per group.

Regions: the top copies from 18 (locus_followup.csv), each widened by 3 kb on both sides so the
flanking LTRs of a provirus are included. Cut sites come straight from the Cell Ranger fragment files
(tabix queries, kept cells only), are summed into the ATAC units and scaled by total cut sites
(per million); group = mean of its units. For each copy: accessibility in its candidate's group vs the
mean of the other groups (log2FC), and the units open (> 2x rest mean).
Also lists the LTR-class elements inside each window (the provirus structure).

Outputs: $TE_OUT/qc/locus_atac.csv
"""
import os
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pysam

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TE_OUT = Path(os.environ["TE_OUT"]); ANNOT = Path(os.environ["ANNOTATION_CSV"]); TE_ANNOT = Path(os.environ["TE_ANNOT_DIR"])
qc = TE_OUT / "qc"; FLANK = 3000
pd.set_option("display.width", 250); pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 300)

fu = pd.read_csv(qc / "locus_followup.csv")
p = fu.locus.str.rsplit("_", n=3, expand=True)
fu["chrom"], fu["start"], fu["end"] = p[0], p[1].astype(int), p[2].astype(int)
regions = fu[["locus", "chrom", "start", "end"]].drop_duplicates("locus").set_index("locus")
regions["w0"] = (regions.start - FLANK).clip(lower=0); regions["w1"] = regions.end + FLANK

samples = pd.read_csv(REPO / "configs/samples.tsv", sep="\t")
ann = pd.read_csv(ANNOT, index_col=0, dtype=str)
ann = ann[ann.include_downstream.str.lower() == "true"]
units = pd.read_csv(TE_OUT / "deseq2/atac/coldata.csv", index_col=0)

counts = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=units.index, columns=regions.index)
for s in samples.itertuples():
    frag = Path(s.atac_bam).parent / "atac_fragments.tsv.gz"
    keep = {c.split("#", 1)[1]: g for c, g in ann.ATAC_WNN_annotation.items() if c.startswith(s.sample + "#")}
    tb = pysam.TabixFile(str(frag))
    for lid, r in regions.iterrows():
        n = {}
        for line in tb.fetch(r.chrom, r.w0, r.w1):
            c, a, b, bc = line.split("\t")[:4]
            g = keep.get(bc)
            if g is None:
                continue
            a, b = int(a), int(b) - 1
            hits = (r.w0 <= a < r.w1) + (r.w0 <= b < r.w1)
            u = f"{s.sample}__{g}"
            n[u] = n.get(u, 0) + hits
        for u, v in n.items():
            if u in counts.index:
                counts.loc[u, lid] += v
    print(f"{s.sample}: done", flush=True)
cpm = counts.div(units.lib_size, axis=0) * 1e6
gm = cpm.groupby(units.group).mean()

# LTR-class elements in each window
rm = pd.read_csv(TE_ANNOT / "rmsk_hg38.bed.gz", sep="\t", header=None, usecols=[0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7],
                 names=["chrom", "start", "end", "sub", "strand", "class"])
rm = rm[rm["class"].str.startswith("LTR")]
struct = {}
for lid, r in regions.iterrows():
    e = rm[(rm.chrom == r.chrom) & (rm.end > r.w0) & (rm.start < r.w1)]
    struct[lid] = " ".join(f"{x.sub}({x.strand})" for x in e.itertuples())

rows = []
for x in fu.itertuples():
    g = x.level
    a = gm.loc[g, x.locus]; rest = gm.drop(g)[x.locus].mean()
    u = cpm.loc[units.group == g, x.locus]
    rows.append({"subfamily": x.subfamily, "level": g, "tier": x.tier, "rank": x.rank, "locus": x.locus,
                 "rna_log2fc": x.log2fc, "atac_cpm_group": a, "atac_cpm_rest": rest,
                 "atac_log2fc": np.log2((a + 0.5) / (rest + 0.5)), "atac_units_open": f"{(u > 2 * rest).sum()}/{len(u)}",
                 "atac_max_group": gm[x.locus].idxmax(), "window_ltrs": struct[x.locus], "context": x.context,
                 "host_gene": x.host_gene})
out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
out.round(3).to_csv(qc / "locus_atac.csv", index=False)
print(out.drop(columns=["window_ltrs"]).round(2).to_string(index=False))
print("done", qc)
scripts/21_herv9_chr5_provirus.py
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
The HERV9 provirus at chr5:30,197,738-30,205,134 (+): RNA and chromatin across cell groups.

Structure (RepeatMasker): LTR12B (5' LTR) - HERV9NC-int - HERV9-int - LTR12_ (3' LTR), ~7.4 kb,
1 Mb from the nearest protein-coding gene (CDH6). The per-copy analysis (16/18/20) showed this one copy
gives ~90-97% of the LTR12_ / HERV9 induction in ENP2 and early endocrine groups.

RNA : IRescue locus counts (sense strand) for the copies of this provirus, per million gene UMIs.
ATAC: Tn5 cut sites from the fragment files in 5 windows (5' LTR +-100 bp, internal 5' / 3' halves,
      3' LTR +-100 bp, 2 kb downstream), per million total cut sites; units -> group means.
Outputs: $TE_OUT/qc/herv9_chr5_provirus.csv, herv9_chr5_provirus.png
"""
import os
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pysam
import scipy.sparse as sp

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TE_OUT = Path(os.environ["TE_OUT"]); ANNOT = Path(os.environ["ANNOTATION_CSV"]); qc = TE_OUT / "qc"
CHROM = "chr5"
WINDOWS = {"5' LTR (LTR12B)": (30197638, 30198283), "internal 5'": (30198283, 30201000),
           "internal 3'": (30201000, 30204661), "3' LTR (LTR12_)": (30204561, 30205234),
           "downstream 2 kb": (30205234, 30207234)}
COPIES = ["LTR12B|chr5_30197738_30198183_+", "HERV9NC-int|chr5_30198183_30203886_+",
          "HERV9-int|chr5_30203884_30204661_+", "LTR12_|chr5_30204661_30205134_+"]
ORDER = ["hPSC", "DE", "GT", "OTX2_endo", "FG", "liver", "PP1", "PP2", "ENP1", "ENP2", "ENP3", "early_SC_beta",
         "early_EC_beta", "early_SC_alpha", "early_SC_delta", "early_SC_EC", "late_SC_beta", "late_EC_beta",
         "late_SC_alpha", "late_SC_EC"]

# ---- RNA, per copy
M = sp.load_npz(TE_OUT / "irescue_locus/locus_units.npz").tocsc()
loci = pd.Index((TE_OUT / "irescue_locus/locus_units_loci.txt").read_text().split("\n"))
ru = pd.read_csv(TE_OUT / "irescue_locus/locus_units_units.csv", index_col=0)
idx = loci.get_indexer(COPIES)
rna = pd.DataFrame(M[:, idx[idx >= 0]].toarray(), index=ru.index, columns=[c for c, i in zip(COPIES, idx) if i >= 0])
rna = rna.div(ru.lib_size, axis=0) * 1e6
rna["provirus total"] = rna.sum(1)
rna_g = rna.groupby(ru.group).mean()

# ---- ATAC, cut sites per window
ann = pd.read_csv(ANNOT, index_col=0, dtype=str)
ann = ann[ann.include_downstream.str.lower() == "true"]
au = pd.read_csv(TE_OUT / "deseq2/atac/coldata.csv", index_col=0)
cnt = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=au.index, columns=list(WINDOWS))
lo = min(w[0] for w in WINDOWS.values()) - 1000; hi = max(w[1] for w in WINDOWS.values()) + 1000
for s in pd.read_csv(REPO / "configs/samples.tsv", sep="\t").itertuples():
    keep = {c.split("#", 1)[1]: g for c, g in ann.ATAC_WNN_annotation.items() if c.startswith(s.sample + "#")}
    tb = pysam.TabixFile(str(Path(s.atac_bam).parent / "atac_fragments.tsv.gz"))
    for line in tb.fetch(CHROM, lo, hi):
        c, a, b, bc = line.split("\t")[:4]
        g = keep.get(bc)
        u = f"{s.sample}__{g}"
        if g is None or u not in cnt.index:
            continue
        for x in (int(a), int(b) - 1):
            for k, (w0, w1) in WINDOWS.items():
                if w0 <= x < w1:
                    cnt.loc[u, k] += 1
atac = cnt.div(au.lib_size, axis=0) * 1e6
atac_g = atac.groupby(au.group).mean()
n_open = (atac.groupby(au.group)["5' LTR (LTR12B)"].apply(lambda v: f"{(v > 2).sum()}/{len(v)}"))

tab = rna_g.add_prefix("RNA ").join(atac_g.add_prefix("ATAC ")).join(n_open.rename("units 5'LTR > 2")).reindex(ORDER)
tab.round(2).to_csv(qc / "herv9_chr5_provirus.csv")
pd.set_option("display.width", 250)
print(tab.round(2).to_string())

fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 4.2))
x = np.arange(len(ORDER))
ax1.bar(x - 0.2, tab["RNA provirus total"], width=0.4, color="#2166ac", label="RNA: provirus copies (sense UMIs per million gene UMIs)")
ax1.set_ylabel("RNA (per million gene UMIs)", color="#2166ac")
ax2 = ax1.twinx()
ax2.bar(x + 0.2, tab["ATAC 5' LTR (LTR12B)"], width=0.4, color="#b2182b", label="ATAC: 5' LTR cut sites (per million)")
ax2.set_ylabel("ATAC, 5' LTR (per million cut sites)", color="#b2182b")
ax1.set_xticks(x, ORDER, rotation=60, ha="right", fontsize=8)
ax1.set_title("HERV9 provirus chr5:30,197,738-30,205,134 (+): LTR12B - HERV9NC/HERV9-int - LTR12_")
h1, l1 = ax1.get_legend_handles_labels(); h2, l2 = ax2.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax1.legend(h1 + h2, l1 + l2, fontsize=8, frameon=False, loc="upper left")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(qc / "herv9_chr5_provirus.png", dpi=110)
print("done", qc)

4.16 Trajectory: provirus vs CDH6 (idea from the phone session)

Idea
The nearest protein-coding gene to the provirus is CDH6 (K-cadherin), ~1 Mb away with nothing protein-coding in between. CDH6 is high in PP and drops at ENP1 → ENP2, where the provirus switches on. Hypothesis: the provirus takes part in, or marks, the adhesion switch as endocrine progenitors delaminate from the PP epithelium. Full note: docs/IDEA_HERV9_CDH6_delamination.md.
How
  1. Cells: PP1/PP2 → ENP1–3 → early endocrine, up to 4,000 per group (27,117 cells).
  2. Pseudotime: diffusion pseudotime on the scVI B latent (X_scvi_scviB_per_sample), rooted at the PP1 extreme of DC1.
  3. Per-cell signals: gene counts from the shared counts layer; provirus RNA from per-copy IRescue counts (4 copies); ATAC cut sites from fragments at the 5′ LTR and at every promoter within ±2 Mb, scaled by cut sites at 20 housekeeping promoters.
  4. Order of events: 40 equal-size pseudotime bins; for each feature, the half-max crossing (switch on / off), with 95% bootstrap intervals over cells.
  5. Cis link: metacells (k-means on the latent within each sample, ~50 cells; 541 metacells). Spearman correlation of provirus RNA and 5′ LTR accessibility with each expressed gene within ±2 Mb, against 1,000 random expressed genes (empirical p).
Run
Job 33438462 (2.5 min). The latent key was passed explicitly; the script's default would have picked scVI A.
scripts/22_herv9_cdh6_trajectory.py
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
HERV9 chr5 provirus vs CDH6 along the PP -> ENP -> endocrine trajectory (idea note:
docs/IDEA_HERV9_CDH6_delamination.md).

Question: does the provirus switch on as CDH6 (and other epithelial adhesion genes) switch off at
ENP1 -> ENP2, i.e. during endocrine delamination? Which comes first, and is the 5' LTR (LTR12B)
accessibility linked to CDH6 or to any other gene in cis?

Steps
  1. Cells: include_downstream == True and ATAC_WNN_annotation in LINEAGE (PP1/PP2 -> ENP1-3 -> early
     endocrine; late groups optional with --with-late). At most --max-per-group cells per group.
  2. Pseudotime: diffusion pseudotime (scanpy) on the scVI latent, root = the PP1 cell at the extreme of
     the first diffusion component on the PP side. Also stores DC1/DC2 for plotting.
  3. Per-cell RNA: gene counts (shared counts layer of the scVI object) for the adhesion / EMT /
     endocrine panel; provirus = IRescue locus counts of the 4 copies (sense), per cell.
  4. Per-cell ATAC: Tn5 cut sites from the fragment files in the provirus 5' LTR, the CDH6 promoter,
     and every promoter (TSS +-1 kb) of protein-coding genes within +-2 Mb; normalised per bin by cut
     sites in a housekeeping-promoter background (no per-cell library size needed).
  5. Pseudotime bins (--n-bins, equal cell numbers): CPM-type means per bin; min-max scaled curves;
     half-max crossing point per feature (rising for provirus, falling for CDH6), with a bootstrap CI
     over cells.
  6. Cis links: metacells (k-means on the latent within each sample, ~--cells-per-metacell cells);
     Spearman of provirus RNA and of 5' LTR accessibility against every expressed gene within +-2 Mb,
     plus a null from --n-null random expressed genes genome-wide (empirical p).

Outputs ($TE_OUT/qc/herv9_cdh6/): cells.csv, trajectory_bins.csv, onset_summary.csv,
cis_links.csv, trajectory.png
Untested draft (2026-10-04): check the CHECK markers below (object paths / obsm key / IRescue
locus file layout) on the first run.
"""
import argparse
import glob
import gzip
import os
from pathlib import Path

import h5py
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pysam
import scipy.io
import scipy.sparse as sp
from scipy.stats import spearmanr

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--with-late", action="store_true", help="also include late endocrine groups")
ap.add_argument("--max-per-group", type=int, default=4000)
ap.add_argument("--n-bins", type=int, default=40)
ap.add_argument("--cells-per-metacell", type=int, default=50)
ap.add_argument("--n-null", type=int, default=1000)
ap.add_argument("--n-boot", type=int, default=200)
ap.add_argument("--latent-key", default=os.environ.get("SCVI_LATENT_KEY", ""))
ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
args = ap.parse_args()
rng = np.random.default_rng(args.seed)

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TE_OUT = Path(os.environ["TE_OUT"]); SCP_OUT = Path(os.environ["SCP_OUT"])
ANNOT = Path(os.environ["ANNOTATION_CSV"]); TE_ANNOT = Path(os.environ["TE_ANNOT_DIR"])
out = TE_OUT / "qc/herv9_cdh6"; out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
pd.set_option("display.width", 250)

LINEAGE = ["PP1", "PP2", "ENP1", "ENP2", "ENP3", "early_SC_beta", "early_EC_beta", "early_SC_alpha",
           "early_SC_delta", "early_SC_EC"]
if args.with_late:
    LINEAGE += ["late_SC_beta", "late_EC_beta", "late_SC_alpha", "late_SC_EC"]
PANEL = ["CDH6", "CDH1", "CDH2", "EPCAM", "CLDN4", "CLDN6", "CLDN7", "SNAI1", "SNAI2", "ZEB1", "ZEB2", "VIM",
         "SOX9", "PDX1", "NKX6-1", "ONECUT1", "NEUROG3", "NEUROD1", "INSM1", "NKX2-2", "CHGA", "INS", "GCG", "SST",
         "TPH1", "DROSHA", "C5orf22"]
CHROM, PROV_START, PROV_END = "chr5", 30197738, 30205134
LTR5 = (30197638, 30198283)                                     # 5' LTR (LTR12B) +-100 bp
COPY_KEYS = ["chr5_30197738_30198183", "chr5_30198183_30203886", "chr5_30203884_30204661",
             "chr5_30204661_30205134"]
CIS = 2_000_000
HOUSEKEEPING = ["GAPDH", "ACTB", "TBP", "PGK1", "RPLP0", "HPRT1", "B2M", "PPIA", "YWHAZ", "SDHA", "UBC",
                "GUSB", "HMBS", "POLR2A", "EEF1A1", "TUBB", "RPL13A", "PSMB2", "VCP", "EIF4A2"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1. cells
ann = pd.read_csv(ANNOT, index_col=0, dtype=str)
ann = ann[(ann.include_downstream.str.lower() == "true") & ann.ATAC_WNN_annotation.isin(LINEAGE)]
ann = ann.groupby("ATAC_WNN_annotation", group_keys=False).apply(
    lambda d: d.sample(min(len(d), args.max_per_group), random_state=args.seed))
print("cells per group:\n", ann.ATAC_WNN_annotation.value_counts().reindex(LINEAGE).to_string(), flush=True)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 2. latent + pseudotime
SCVI_H5AD = SCP_OUT / "integration/h5ad/merged_rna_scvi_integrated.h5ad"     # CHECK: or scvi_filtered/


def find_latent(f):
    keys = list(f["obsm"].keys())
    if args.latent_key:
        return args.latent_key
    pref = [k for k in keys if "scvi" in k.lower() and "umap" not in k.lower()]
    if not pref:
        raise SystemExit(f"no scVI latent in obsm: {keys}; pass --latent-key")
    print("obsm keys:", keys, "-> using", pref[0], flush=True)
    return pref[0]


with h5py.File(SCVI_H5AD, "r") as f:
    cells_all = pd.Index(f["obs"]["_index"][:].astype(str))
    key = find_latent(f)
    sel = cells_all.get_indexer(ann.index)
    keep = sel >= 0
    ann = ann[keep]; sel = sel[keep]
    order = np.argsort(sel)
    lat = f["obsm"][key][np.sort(sel)]
    ann = ann.iloc[order]
    var = pd.Index(f["var"]["_index"][:].astype(str))
    # per-cell gene counts (raw counts layer, CSR) for the panel + all genes we may need later
    L = f["layers"]["counts"]; indptr = L["indptr"][:]
    rows = np.sort(sel)
    lib = np.zeros(len(rows), dtype=np.float64)
    data_blocks, ind_blocks, ptr = [], [], [0]
    for k, r in enumerate(rows):
        a, b = indptr[r], indptr[r + 1]
        d = L["data"][a:b]; i = L["indices"][a:b]
        lib[k] = d.sum(); data_blocks.append(d); ind_blocks.append(i); ptr.append(ptr[-1] + len(d))
    X = sp.csr_matrix((np.concatenate(data_blocks), np.concatenate(ind_blocks), np.array(ptr)),
                      shape=(len(rows), len(var)))
cells = ann.index
group = ann.ATAC_WNN_annotation.values
sample = np.array([c.split("#")[0] for c in cells])
print(f"{len(cells)} cells, latent {key} {lat.shape}", flush=True)

import anndata as ad
import scanpy as sc
A = ad.AnnData(X=np.zeros((len(cells), 1), dtype=np.float32), obs=pd.DataFrame({"group": group}, index=cells))
A.obsm["X_lat"] = np.asarray(lat, dtype=np.float32)
sc.pp.neighbors(A, use_rep="X_lat", n_neighbors=30)
sc.tl.diffmap(A, n_comps=10)
dc1 = A.obsm["X_diffmap"][:, 1]
pp_side = np.sign(np.median(dc1[group == "PP1"]) - np.median(dc1[np.isin(group, ["early_EC_beta", "early_SC_beta"])]))
cand = np.where(group == "PP1")[0]
A.uns["iroot"] = int(cand[np.argmax(pp_side * dc1[cand])])
sc.tl.dpt(A)
pt = A.obs["dpt_pseudotime"].values
print("median pseudotime per group:\n", pd.Series(pt).groupby(group).median().reindex(LINEAGE).round(3).to_string(), flush=True)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3. provirus RNA per cell
# CHECK: assumes IRescue locus output per sample at $TE_OUT/irescue_locus/<sample>/counts/
#        {barcodes,features}.tsv.gz + matrix.mtx.gz (features x cells, 10x style)
prov = pd.Series(0.0, index=cells)
for s in np.unique(sample):
    d = TE_OUT / "irescue_locus" / s / "counts"
    if not d.exists():
        print("missing", d, flush=True); continue
    bc = pd.read_csv(d / "barcodes.tsv.gz", header=None)[0].astype(str).values
    feat = pd.read_csv(d / "features.tsv.gz", header=None, sep="\t")[0].astype(str).values
    fi = [k for k, x in enumerate(feat) if any(c in x for c in COPY_KEYS)]
    if not fi:
        print("provirus copies not found in", d, flush=True); continue
    m = scipy.io.mmread(d / "matrix.mtx.gz").tocsr()
    if m.shape[0] != len(feat):
        m = m.T.tocsr()
    v = np.asarray(m[fi].sum(0)).ravel()
    s_cells = pd.Series(v, index=[f"{s}#{b}" for b in bc])
    prov.update(s_cells.reindex(cells).dropna())

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 4. genes: GTF, cis window, TSSs
rows_g = []
with open(TE_ANNOT / "scte/genes.gtf") as fh:
    for line in fh:
        if line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        t = line.split("\t", 9)
        if t[2] != "gene":
            continue
        a = t[8]
        name = a.split('gene_name "')[1].split('"')[0]
        gtype = a.split('gene_type "')[1].split('"')[0] if 'gene_type "' in a else ""
        tss = int(t[3]) - 1 if t[6] == "+" else int(t[4]) - 1
        rows_g.append((t[0], int(t[3]) - 1, int(t[4]), name, gtype, t[6], tss))
genes = pd.DataFrame(rows_g, columns=["chrom", "start", "end", "gene", "type", "strand", "tss"]).drop_duplicates("gene")
cis = genes[(genes.chrom == CHROM) & (genes.end > PROV_START - CIS) & (genes.start < PROV_END + CIS)]
print("genes within 2 Mb:", ", ".join(cis.gene), flush=True)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 5. ATAC cut sites per cell
windows = {"prov_5LTR": (CHROM, *LTR5)}
for g in cis.itertuples():
    windows[f"tss_{g.gene}"] = (g.chrom, g.tss - 1000, g.tss + 1000)
hk = genes[genes.gene.isin(HOUSEKEEPING)]
for g in hk.itertuples():
    windows[f"hk_{g.gene}"] = (g.chrom, g.tss - 1000, g.tss + 1000)
wnames = list(windows)
acc = np.zeros((len(cells), len(wnames)), dtype=np.float32)
cpos = {c: k for k, c in enumerate(cells)}
st = pd.read_csv(REPO / "configs/samples.tsv", sep="\t")
for s in st.itertuples():
    if s.sample not in set(sample):
        continue
    tb = pysam.TabixFile(str(Path(s.atac_bam).parent / "atac_fragments.tsv.gz"))     # as in script 21
    for j, w in enumerate(wnames):
        ch, a0, a1 = windows[w]
        try:
            it = tb.fetch(ch, max(0, a0 - 1000), a1 + 1000)
        except ValueError:
            continue
        for line in it:
            c, a, b, bc = line.split("\t")[:4]
            k = cpos.get(f"{s.sample}#{bc}")
            if k is None:
                continue
            for x in (int(a), int(b) - 1):
                if a0 <= x < a1:
                    acc[k, j] += 1
acc = pd.DataFrame(acc, index=cells, columns=wnames)
hk_cols = [w for w in wnames if w.startswith("hk_")]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- per-cell table
panel = [g for g in PANEL if g in var]
gi = var.get_indexer(panel)
expr = pd.DataFrame(X[:, gi].toarray(), index=cells, columns=panel)
cell_tab = pd.DataFrame({"group": group, "sample": sample, "pseudotime": pt, "DC1": dc1,
                         "DC2": A.obsm["X_diffmap"][:, 2], "gene_umis": lib, "provirus": prov.values}, index=cells)
cell_tab = cell_tab.join(expr).join(acc[["prov_5LTR"] + [w for w in wnames if w == "tss_CDH6"]])
cell_tab["hk_cutsites"] = acc[hk_cols].sum(1).values
cell_tab.to_csv(out / "cells.csv")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 6. pseudotime bins + onset
cell_tab["bin"] = pd.qcut(cell_tab.pseudotime.rank(method="first"), args.n_bins, labels=False)


def bin_means(t):
    g = t.groupby("bin")
    res = pd.DataFrame({"pseudotime": g.pseudotime.median(), "n": g.size()})
    lib_b = g.gene_umis.sum()
    for c in ["provirus"] + panel:
        res[c] = g[c].sum() / lib_b * 1e6
    hk_b = g.hk_cutsites.sum().clip(lower=1)
    res["ATAC_prov_5LTR"] = g.prov_5LTR.sum() / hk_b * 1e3
    if "tss_CDH6" in t:
        res["ATAC_CDH6_promoter"] = g.tss_CDH6.sum() / hk_b * 1e3
    comp = pd.crosstab(t.bin, t.group, normalize="index")
    return res, comp


bins, comp = bin_means(cell_tab)
bins.join(comp.add_prefix("frac_")).round(4).to_csv(out / "trajectory_bins.csv")

FEATURES = {"provirus": "rise", "ATAC_prov_5LTR": "rise", "CDH6": "fall", "CDH1": "fall", "EPCAM": "fall",
            "SOX9": "fall", "NEUROG3": "rise", "NEUROD1": "rise", "CHGA": "rise", "SNAI2": "rise"}
if "ATAC_CDH6_promoter" in bins:
    FEATURES["ATAC_CDH6_promoter"] = "fall"


def halfmax(b, col, direction):
    y = b[col].rolling(3, center=True, min_periods=1).mean().values
    x = b.pseudotime.values
    lo_, hi_ = np.nanmin(y), np.nanmax(y)
    if hi_ - lo_ <= 0:
        return np.nan
    z = (y - lo_) / (hi_ - lo_)
    if direction == "rise":
        k = np.argmax(z >= 0.5)
    else:
        start = np.argmax(z)                        # fall after the peak
        after = np.where(z[start:] <= 0.5)[0]
        if not len(after):
            return np.nan
        k = start + after[0]
    return x[k]


feats = {c: d for c, d in FEATURES.items() if c in bins}
boot = {c: [] for c in feats}
for _ in range(args.n_boot):                      # resample cells, keep each cell's original bin
    t = cell_tab.sample(len(cell_tab), replace=True, random_state=int(rng.integers(1e9)))
    b, _ = bin_means(t)
    for c, d in feats.items():
        boot[c].append(halfmax(b, c, d))
onset = [{"feature": c, "direction": d, "halfmax_pt": halfmax(bins, c, d),
          "ci_lo": np.nanpercentile(boot[c], 2.5), "ci_hi": np.nanpercentile(boot[c], 97.5)}
         for c, d in feats.items()]
onset = pd.DataFrame(onset).sort_values("halfmax_pt")
onset.round(4).to_csv(out / "onset_summary.csv", index=False)
print("half-max crossing along pseudotime (rise = switch on, fall = switch off):\n", onset.round(3).to_string(index=False), flush=True)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 7. metacells + cis links
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
mc = pd.Series("", index=cells)
for s in np.unique(sample):
    ix = np.where(sample == s)[0]
    k = max(1, len(ix) // args.cells_per_metacell)
    lab = KMeans(n_clusters=k, n_init=4, random_state=args.seed).fit_predict(np.asarray(lat)[ix]) if k > 1 else np.zeros(len(ix), int)
    mc.iloc[ix] = [f"{s}_m{x}" for x in lab]
M = sp.csr_matrix((np.ones(len(cells)), (pd.factorize(mc)[0], np.arange(len(cells)))))
mc_names = pd.factorize(mc)[1]
G = M @ X                                                     # metacell x gene counts
mlib = np.asarray(G.sum(1)).ravel()
expressed = np.where(np.asarray((G > 0).sum(0)).ravel() >= 0.2 * G.shape[0])[0]
mprov = M @ prov.values / mlib * 1e6
macc = (M @ acc.values)
mhk = macc[:, [wnames.index(w) for w in hk_cols]].sum(1).clip(min=1)
mltr = macc[:, wnames.index("prov_5LTR")] / mhk * 1e3


def gene_cpm(j):
    return np.asarray(G[:, j].todense()).ravel() / mlib * 1e6


null_j = rng.choice(expressed, size=min(args.n_null, len(expressed)), replace=False)
null_rna = np.array([spearmanr(mprov, gene_cpm(j))[0] for j in null_j])
null_acc = np.array([spearmanr(mltr, gene_cpm(j))[0] for j in null_j])
links = []
for g in cis.itertuples():
    if g.gene not in var:
        continue
    j = var.get_loc(g.gene)
    if j not in set(expressed):
        continue
    y = gene_cpm(j)
    r1 = spearmanr(mprov, y)[0]; r2 = spearmanr(mltr, y)[0]
    tsscol = f"tss_{g.gene}"
    r3 = spearmanr(mltr, macc[:, wnames.index(tsscol)] / mhk)[0] if tsscol in wnames else np.nan
    links.append({"gene": g.gene, "type": g.type, "dist_kb": round((g.tss - PROV_START) / 1000),
                  "rho_provRNA_gene": r1, "p_emp_rna": (np.sum(np.abs(null_rna) >= abs(r1)) + 1) / (len(null_rna) + 1),
                  "rho_5LTRacc_gene": r2, "p_emp_acc": (np.sum(np.abs(null_acc) >= abs(r2)) + 1) / (len(null_acc) + 1),
                  "rho_5LTRacc_promoterAcc": r3})
links = pd.DataFrame(links).sort_values("rho_provRNA_gene")
links.round(4).to_csv(out / "cis_links.csv", index=False)
print(f"\n{len(mc_names)} metacells; cis links (+-2 Mb), empirical p vs {len(null_j)} random genes:\n",
      links.round(3).to_string(index=False), flush=True)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 8. figure
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(17, 4.6), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.2, 1.6, 1]})
ax = axs[0]
cmap = plt.get_cmap("tab20")
for k, g in enumerate(LINEAGE):
    m = group == g
    if m.any():
        ax.scatter(dc1[m], cell_tab.DC2.values[m], s=2, color=cmap(k % 20), label=g, rasterized=True)
ax.set_xlabel("DC1"); ax.set_ylabel("DC2"); ax.set_title("diffusion map (scVI latent)")
ax.legend(fontsize=6, markerscale=4, frameon=False, ncol=2)
ax = axs[1]
for col, c in [("provirus", "#b2182b"), ("ATAC_prov_5LTR", "#ef8a62"), ("CDH6", "#2166ac"),
               ("ATAC_CDH6_promoter", "#67a9cf"), ("CDH1", "#4d9221"), ("NEUROG3", "#762a83"), ("CHGA", "#999999")]:
    if col in bins:
        y = bins[col].rolling(3, center=True, min_periods=1).mean()
        ax.plot(bins.pseudotime, (y - y.min()) / (y.max() - y.min() + 1e-12), color=c, label=col,
                lw=2.2 if col in ("provirus", "CDH6") else 1.2)
ax.set_xlabel("diffusion pseudotime (PP1 root)"); ax.set_ylabel("scaled (bin means, min-max)")
ax.set_title("provirus vs CDH6 along PP -> ENP -> endocrine"); ax.legend(fontsize=7, frameon=False)
ax = axs[2]
if len(links):
    ax.barh(links.gene, links.rho_provRNA_gene, color=["#2166ac" if g == "CDH6" else "#bbbbbb" for g in links.gene])
    lo_, hi_ = np.percentile(null_rna, [2.5, 97.5])
    ax.axvspan(lo_, hi_, color="#fddbc7", alpha=0.6, label="95% random genes")
    ax.set_xlabel("Spearman, provirus RNA vs gene (metacells)"); ax.set_title("cis genes +-2 Mb")
    ax.legend(fontsize=7, frameon=False); ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=7)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(out / "trajectory.png", dpi=120)
print("done", out)

5. What we learned so far

5.0 What is already known (and what is not)

Finding in our dataPublishedStatus for us
HERVH-int / LTR7 high in hPSC, falling quickly after exit from pluripotencyTextbook. HERVH also "switches" to different, endoderm-specific transcripts in DE (Babarinde et al., Nat Commun 2025, 16:7670).positive control
HERVS71-int and its LTRs LTR6A/B transcribed and opened in DE / GT / OTX2_endo, peak at D4Wu et al., Cell Rep 2022 (41:111791): LTR6B and related ERVs act as DE enhancers with FOXA2 / GATA4 sites, are unlocked by TET1-mediated demethylation, and drive primate-specific ERBB4 expression. Babarinde et al. 2025: LTR6A-containing non-coding transcripts are endoderm-specific (72–96 h), transient, and not kept in hepatocytes.positive control Our D4 peak and later fall match both papers.
MER11A/B/C (LTRs of HERVK11) and pancreatic fateDe Franco et al., Nat Genet 2023: ZNF808 represses MER11. Its loss activates MER11 copies during pancreas differentiation, liver genes come on, and the result is pancreatic agenesis.Tested in 5.9: no sign of ZNF808 failure in our liver-like cells at subfamily level.
ERV programs in pancreatic progenitors, endocrine progenitors and endocrine cells (HERV15/LTR15, LTR12/HERV9, LTR22, MLT1F2)Nothing found in a Europe PMC keyword search (TE/ERV × pancreas/islet/beta cell × development, cancer excluded). The only developmental hit was the ZNF808 paper. The search was not exhaustive.apparently new

5.1 Global TE load is flat across stages

The median cell has about as many TE UMIs as half its gene UMIs, which is typical for nuclei: most of it is intronic SINE/LINE signal. The TE load and the class mix barely change across the time course. LINEs rise slightly and SINEs fall slightly at D22–D45. There is no global "ERV de-repression" during differentiation, so any signal will be specific subfamilies in specific cells.

5.5 The read-through filter changes the picture (today's result)

Only about 21% of LTR-class TE reads come from copies outside genes (nointron ÷ exclusive). For SINEs and DNA transposons it is about 10%. Fold changes agree well between IRescue and scTE-exclusive (r = 0.82), so the two counting methods agree. They agree much less between exclusive and nointron (r = 0.45), which is the read-through effect. Of 242 LTR calls from IRescue or exclusive: 129 intergenic, 45 weak, 29 too few reads outside genes to test, 39 intronic only.

Robust: supported by copies outside genes
  • HERVH-int, LTR7/7Y, HERVS71-int, HERVK11-int, LTR6B in hPSC → DE → GT → FG → OTX2_endo
  • LTR12_ / LTR12E / HERV9(NC)-int in ENP1–3 and early endocrine. Their share of reads from outside genes rises to 0.8–0.9 in these groups (frac_ratio 1.2–1.7).
  • MLT1F2-int in ENP1–3 (MER110-int there is up in scTE and nointron but not in IRescue, which counts only the TE's own strand, so it is probably antisense; see 5.8)
  • LTR60B in early β / EC-β
  • liver: HERVIP10B3, HERVI, PABL_A/B, LTR10B1/B2/E
Read-through suspects: gone in nointron
  • MER92-int (late β, late/early EC-β, D22/D45): nointron log2FC −0.9 to −0.1; only 3–7% of reads come from outside genes in those groups
  • MER110-int in late β / EC-β (its ENP signal is real)
  • LTR48B (ENP1/2, D15), LTR19C and LTR25-int (PP2, D12/D15)
  • HERVK-int in OTX2_endo; HERVE-int in hPSC; HERV4_I-int at D0
  • LTR21A, Harlequin-int, LTR19C in liver / stroma
HERV15-int in PP1/PP2: mixed, top locus-level candidate. It is still significantly up in nointron (log2FC 1.5 in PP1, 1.7 in PP2, padj < 0.05). That is far below IRescue's 3.4 / 4.5. In PP2 only 9% of its reads come from copies outside genes, vs 34% elsewhere (frac_ratio 0.26). The PP increase therefore has a real component outside genes plus a larger contribution from copies inside genes, probably one or a few host genes active in pancreatic progenitors. Supporting the real component: LTR15, HERV15's LTR (confirmed from genome flanks, 4.12), is more accessible in PP2 (log2FC 2.2 cut sites / 1.9 scTEATAC) and PP1 (1.4 / 1.2).

5.7 ATAC: cut sites and scTEATAC agree

  • Fold changes: r = 0.95 across groups and r = 0.96 across stages. Per-subfamily totals correlate at r = 0.99 (log scale).
  • Calls: 462 by cut sites, 383 by scTEATAC, 337 by both. Almost every call made by one method only is a near-miss: log2FC 0.8–1.0 and significant in the other method. The rest come from the 52-cell ductal group (22 LTR calls by cut sites only).
  • Low-MAPQ reads raise counts only for young non-ERV families: L1HS 2.5×, SVA_E/F 2.2–2.4×, MADE1 3.3×, Alu 2.1×. ERV families show no gain (LTR5_Hs 0.91, HERVK-int 0.81, LTR7 0.89, HERVH-int 0.78; ratios below 1 reflect one count per fragment vs two cut sites).
  • Conclusion: cut sites stay the main ATAC measure, as the more precise accessibility readout. scTEATAC is the confirmation. ATAC support in the tiers counts either method.

5.9 ZNF808 / MER11: no sign of ZNF808 failure in the liver-like cells (subfamily level)

  • ZNF808 is not lower in the liver-like cells. It is 1.4–1.6× higher than in PP1/PP2/FG (21 vs 13–15 per million gene UMIs). TRIM28 is similar. ZNF808 is lowest in late endocrine groups (8–9).
  • MER11 is not specifically active in liver. MER11A/B/C RNA and ATAC are highest in hPSC and early endoderm and fall afterwards. Liver vs PP ratios are 0.7–1.6 with no consistent direction. MER11C is less open in liver (0.73–0.78×).
  • No anti-correlation between ZNF808 and MER11 across groups (Spearman ρ from −0.32 to +0.33 over 20 comparisons).
  • Per copy (19): also negative. Only 2 MER11A copies are "liver-on" (liver ≥ 2 CPM, ≥ 4× the maximum of PP1/PP2/FG, in at least half of the liver units):
    • one in an exon of ZG16, i.e. part of that gene's transcript;
    • one in an intronic lncRNA 112 kb from AHR.
    Too few MER11 copies are expressed at all (fewer than 20 at ≥ 2 CPM) for MER11 to enter the subfamily ranking. Our liver-like cells do not look like ZNF808 loss. A remaining test would be the exact knockout-responsive copies from De Franco et al.'s supplement.

The provirus is an annotated, spliced lncRNA in current Ensembl. ENSG00000297849 (lncRNA, "novel transcript", source havana_tagene, i.e. the GENCODE long-read pipeline), chr5:30,197,989–30,205,018 (+). It has one transcript, ENST00000751379, with 2 exons:
  • exon 1, 30,197,989–30,198,214: starts inside the LTR12B 5′ LTR;
  • exon 2, 30,204,416–30,205,018: the end of HERV9-int into the LTR12_ 3′ LTR.
So it is an LTR-promoted transcript, spliced from the 5′ LTR to the 3′ LTR. Our 10x 3′ reads land on exon 2, matching where IRescue placed most of the signal. Our pipeline called it "intergenic" only because the Cell Ranger 2020-A GTF (GENCODE v32) predates this model. Checked via the Ensembl REST API.

  • Order of events: EPCAM (0.29) and CDH1 (0.36) fall first. Then CDH6 falls together with the NEUROG3 rise (both 0.48). NEUROD1 (0.76) and CHGA (0.86) follow. Only then do the 5′ LTR open (0.89) and the provirus RNA rise (0.90). The provirus switches on after delamination and after CHGA, in committed endocrine cells.
  • No cis link to CDH6: across metacells CDH6 is the most anti-correlated gene within 2 Mb (ρ = −0.55), but random genes genome-wide do as well about 10% of the time (empirical p = 0.10). DROSHA and a lncRNA nearby behave similarly. The 5′ LTR's accessibility is only weakly related to the CDH6 promoter's (ρ = −0.24). Anti-correlation along a lineage is expected for many gene pairs.
  • Revised view: the provirus is a marker of the endocrine state, switched on with or just after CHGA and highest in EC-β and δ. It is not an element of the PP → endocrine adhesion switch. Whether it does anything locally is open: it is a spliced lncRNA, but no nearby gene follows it.
  • Caveats:
    • Pseudotime shape: ENP1 forms its own arm on the diffusion map, so pseudotime between PP and endocrine is not one straight path. With equal-cell bins, few bins fall between 0.3 and 0.75.
    • Confidence intervals: wide for CDH6 (0.47–0.76) and SNAI2, but even CDH6's upper bound is well before the provirus (0.89–0.90).
    • Design limits: one protocol; stage and batch are confounded.

6. Caveats to keep in mind

  • Optimistic p-values. Without a sample term, units from the same sample are not independent, and stage, batch and cell type are confounded. Rank by effect size and by agreement between RNA, nointron and ATAC rather than by padj.
  • Tiny groups (late_SC_delta 42 cells in units, ductal 52, exocrine 121, early_SC_delta 223, stroma 223) give unstable calls. ductal produces 37 ATAC calls from 2 units. These groups should be flagged or excluded.
  • Nointron is strict. A real ERV promoter inside an intron, for example an LTR that drives an alternative first exon of its host gene, is also dropped in nointron. "intronic_only" means "cannot tell at subfamily level", not "proven artefact".
  • scTE is not strand-aware for TEs but IRescue is. That explains part of the higher exclusive counts (e.g. MER110-int 5.6× IRescue) and the "scTE only" calls. Antisense is a hypothesis until the per-copy strand check.
  • ATAC normalisation uses total cut sites only. Groups with different signal-to-noise (TSS enrichment) shift all TE subfamilies together; liver, OTX2_endo, stroma and ductal have many calls. A GC- and accessibility-matched background (chromVAR-style) would be more robust.
  • Novelty rests on a keyword literature search. Before writing, check the pancreas / islet single-cell TE literature more carefully, including preprints.
  • Subfamily ≠ locus. A subfamily call can be driven by a single active copy. Biological claims need the locus level.
  • The README still describes the original plan (sample blocking, chromVAR). The analysis as run uses ~ group and cut-site counts. The README should be updated.

7. Next steps

  1. (done) Provirus vs CDH6, see 5.11: no link, so the delamination hypothesis is dropped. The provirus is an endocrine-state marker.
  2. Fetal pancreas replication (in progress): Olaniru et al. 2023 (GSE197064, 12–20 PCW, 4 hashtag pools, 10x 3′ v3).
    • Download to scratch, then Cell Ranger 9 (GRCh38-2020-A, BAM kept).
    • Reproduce their Seurat analysis: HTODemux plus their published donor/PCW calls, their QC thresholds, SCTransform + integration, annotation.
    • Make it TE-ready: IRescue subfamily and per-copy counts. Is the chr5 HERV9 provirus on in fetal NEUROG3+ progenitors and endocrine cells?
  3. (done) Name the copies, see 5.10. Follow-ups:
    • chr5 HERV9 provirus: what does its transcript look like? Check where reads fall along it, whether it is spliced or polyadenylated, and whether any public long-read or islet data show it. Is it expressed in primary human islets or fetal pancreas endocrine cells? Which TFs bind its LTR12B (NEUROG3, NEUROD1, RFX, NKX2-2 motifs; NF-Y)? Does it affect anything nearby (Hi-C or co-accessibility)? Knockdown or LTR deletion would test function.
    • HERV15 / ACSM3: does the PP ACSM3 transcript start in the LTR15? Look at read coverage, then GENCODE / long-read isoforms.
  4. (done, negative) ZNF808 per copy. Optional: test the exact knockout-responsive MER11 copies from De Franco 2023 supplementary tables.
  5. Regulatory context. Using the diff-multiome group peak set (pending in the pipeline chat), test TE-family enrichment in cell-type peaks. Then look for TF motifs inside the induced or opened LTRs:
    • LTR12_/LTR12E: NF-Y? endocrine TFs?
    • LTR22/LTR22B: NEUROD1, RFX, NKX2-2?
    • LTR15: PP TFs (PDX1, SOX9, ONECUT1)?
    LTR6 serves as the known control (FOXA2/GATA4).
  6. Housekeeping. Flag or exclude tiny groups (ductal, late_SC_delta, exocrine). Redraw the ERV heatmap with tiers. Update the README to match the methods actually used. Commit scripts 05b and 12–17.

Gotchas already solved

  • scTE 'rU' file mode fails on Python 3.11, so it is patched to 'r' in the env build.
  • scTE needs BAMs filtered to whitelisted cells with a corrected UMI.
  • scTE workers each load the full index, so it must run on amem (QoS mem-normal, large memory request).
  • scTEATAC reads barcodes from read names, and bamToBed -bedpe needs name-sorted input. Fixed by prefixing read names with the CB tag and name-sorting (05b_scte_atac.sb).
  • config.sh does not export: use set -a; source config.sh; set +a for Python.
  • acompile needs QoS compile (for env builds with internet access).
